analysis.name: Salam Aboulhassan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The content isn't hard, but the tests are difficult. The multiple choice portion of the tests are hard to get right. You can read the whole reading and understand it and still feel like two options in the multiple choice are right, and this doesn't just happen sometimes, it happens all of the time. Lots of readings, but they were interesting.

I disliked the way she speaks to you during office hours and her common response of "everything's in the lecture." She says one small thing and expects you to remember it for an exam. Still, shes passionate in what she does and I enjoyed listening to her lectures, I just had multiple bad experiences with a passive aggressive attitude.

Prof Aboulhassan was one of the most inspirational professors I've had. Her lectures were always entertaining and inspirational and the readings made me want to learn more outside of the class. The quizzes are pretty hard and you have to pay attention to details of all the readings. Overall loved her and would recommend for an intro soc class!

Salam's lectures are great and really informative. There is a lot of reading, but GSIs explain it clearly, and it's not difficult information. The exams correlate with the readings and her lectures, and they aren't difficult. The final paper was an interesting process, and I enjoyed writing it. Overall, she's a great lecturer and cares a lot.

She is very passionate for what she teaches about and helps you learn about sociology in a fun way! She likes to make jokes during lectures and make the content understandable, especially when readings can be heavy at times. She worked with me through a difficult life period and allowed me to thrive in her class, definitely take!

analysis.name: Anthony Vecchiarelli
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I was disappointed that he read right off of the slides during lecture. Sometimes exam questions asked niche questions that were a sentence on one slide (“what type of engineering is this similar to”). I appreciated that he tried to crack jokes and showed us videos pertaining to what we were learning to try and connect all of the dots.

Dr. V is by far the best + most helpful professor I've had at UMICH! He genuinely cares about his students and is always happy to help, no matter the circumstance. His lectures are clear, and everything you need is on the slides. The exams are super fair and straightforward. Plus, he's just an overall kind and amazing professor. Highly recommend!

Lectures can get boring at times, but overall is engaging and clear. Exams and his "two of the above" questions are... not fun. Pay attention to every detail and you will do fine. He also provides extra credit for attending lecture.
I honestly really enjoyed Dr.V he tries to explain things in simpler ways and tries to crack jokes. I really enjoyed him because he is very inspirational.

I loved Dr. V! Exams can be a little tricky, but if you know the slides, you will do well. If you go to his office hours, he will tell you some of the content on the exam at the end so be sure to go! Great class though and I found it to be an easy A.

analysis.name: Audrey Bennett
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Second class... first class Typography where we designed compositions for her book - and now designing work for another member of her family in Branding. Prepare to experience her haughtiness and superiority with poorly planned classes.

Overall I got a good grade at the end of the class, sometimes things were not clarified in how they were graded. She gives lots of feedback if you ask for it and it's helpful. She also gives plenty of in class time to work on projects so take advantage of that. She is also very nice!

Took me several weeks to figure out that she didn't actually hate us all and could be quite friendly and encouraging, just with a very calm professional demeanor that came off as cold. She does things very by the book. Had some of the best critiques ever in her class, though. Mixed bag for me but really depends on if her teaching style is for you.

Audrey sets up her class by letting student figure out the assignments for themselves, which can be intimidating at first. Her humor is very dry and she can seem scary, but is actually extremely amicable and cares a lot for her students. She loves to interact and give feedback, and her critiques are incredible.
I learned more watching youtube videos - than from her "teaching".

analysis.name: Alex Poniatowski
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 200 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: It is clear that Poniatowski knows a great deal about this subject, but often seems to forget that none of us have a degree in chemistry and rarely spends time explaining concepts. He also has random temper tantrums that are very distracting and condescending. He never cleans the chalkboards properly which is super annoying.

I've never seen a instructor who's five minutes late for almost all the lectures and office hours, making the concepts more confusing, and not willing to help students. Orgo isn't easy. If you want to learn something from the lectures instead of googling everything and learning it all by yourself at home, then don't take it with him!
i ended up just skipping his lecture and going to bartley's instead for the majority of the time. he's funny but is not good at teaching chem unfortunately

Dr. Poniatowski is very energetic and entertaining. However, he doesn't hit everything that needs to be covered for the course and can get sidetracked. I liked the way he explained things, but I had to start going to Bartley's lectures to get all of the information. My grade got a lot better when I switched. Overall very nice guy.

Although he's a good lecturer, the format in which he teaches the class is unnecessarily confusing and annoying to follow. He's a rude guy who doesn't seem to understand that students have many classes and puts in very little extra effort for the class past lectures. Hope he puts in effort in the future and makes handouts or anything for students.

analysis.name: Amy Gottfried
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 229 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: One of my favorite professors at Michigan. She teaches clearly and makes lecture engaging. She provides tons of opportunities to ask questions in person and online, and always makes a point to be thorough, as well as make sure all students have the opportunity to ask their questions. Dr. G's class took heavy commitment but was extremely rewarding.

While Gottfried appears to be nice superficially, her exams are simply too difficult, and the class is even worse than orgo in that she teaches you extremely easy barebones stuff, and you literally teach yourself essentially everything else. There is really no point in paying for this course when I have legitimately taught myself all the material.

Gottfried is the only thing that made PChem bearable. She's one of the most committed professors on campus and wants to help her students. Her exams are extremely difficult, but she holds so many office hours to help us understand the material. This would probably be my least favorite course if any other professor taught it.

Dr. Gottfried is an incredible professor. Although this is debatably the hardest pre-med class at the University of Michigan, she explains everything in a way that makes sense. She seems to genuinely want her students to succeed. That being said, her exams are extremely difficult, but she does curve them. Would not take Pchem with any other prof.

Chem 230 is a tough class but Dr. Gottfried makes it enjoyable and provides lots of resources to aid you throughout the semester.   Piazza was very interactive and she would provide immediate feedback (within 24 hours). She also scheduled lots of office hours.  As long as you start the PREP 7 days+ prior to the exam, it's very doable.

analysis.name: Aaron Burch
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Aaron is a great instructor, chill/funny guy. He interacts well with students. This class really emphasizes the writing process, not just the essays themselves. Your grade is based off attendance/participation, essays, and some short writing assignments/annotated readings, pretty light workload. Definitely take this class with him if you can.

Really cool guy. Can be a tough grader. You have to be able to identify what he's looking for in essays or you'll do poorly, but it wasn't too hard to catch on. Overall, a great professor; I'd take a class of his again. And it's a REALLY good idea to go to office hours if you're struggling with a paper (saved me)!!

Would highly recommend this professor and class to anyone! Aaron Burch is very chill and engaging and you can tell he truly loves what he does and likes to get students excited about their writing. Took this class just because I needed ULWR and I feel like I learned a lot more than I thought I would. Not super tough, but you need to put in effort.

I've had Aaron Burch before for another class, too, and he was great in both of them He's big on group discussion, peer editing, and sharing work, so be ready for that!  If you like to not turn in tiny assignments, you may get in a bit of trouble because the small writing exercises for credit can add up. He's very comfortable and willing to chat!

Cool dude who I found really relatable. Wants class to participate. My section had a lot of people who slacked off so it made it awkward sometimes. There were a few moments where he literally just asked us why so few of us participated. Really passionate about writing and just wants students who care about it as much as he does was what I felt.

analysis.name: Aradhna Krishna
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took Aradhna Krishnas Sensory marketing class because it was the only one available in the B-school world. Theress no question of Krishnas intelligence & research abilities. She has a lot of information & experience to share. However, she has an attitude problem & isnt an effective teacher because of her hubris. I didnt learn much from her.
If you have her drop. Her lectures have no structure and she cold calls when you can tell the whole class is confused.

Mean-spirited and nasty individual. Does not know much about the 'real world' of marketing. In fact, she gets very defensive if you know more 'real-world' marketing than her. I learned nothing new in her class. She is so full of herself!!!
Awful human being. Yells at students for leaving class for any reason (i.e. bathroom, sneeze attack..etc.) On good days her attitude towards students is tolerable at best. On bad days...watch out.

Fantastic professor! Extremely intelligent and informed about her industry. Very engaging in class; wants her students to pay attention and will call you out if you're not. There's no reason not to pay attention, though, because she makes class entertaining and fills lectures with fascinating content. Very accommodating to student needs, too.

analysis.name: Alexander Ganago
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 81 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ganago is that grandpa that wants to teach you but can't fully articulate a complete sentence anymore. He will email you 3-4 emails a day talking about his emails he sent you the day before. Lectures are useless unless you need to catch up on sleep. It's an easy A if you put in the work outside of class. He is a horrible professor, good luck

- Senile
- Cannot hear
- Does not understand what is going on around him
- 60 page labs that have to be completed in two hours
- Canvas is extremely unorganized
- Extremely rude
- Tells you to buy his own textbook which you will never use
- Do not go to lecture, just read his slides to not waste your time, all of the material is taught in Physics 2

Ganago is a genuinely nice guy - he wants you to learn! But he does not teach well. The course pack is pretty much how you teach yourself this class. Be prepared for 10+ hoursweek doing reading, the homework, multiple test centers, a pre lab, a post lab, etc. Overall a horrible way to learn circuits, but it is pretty easy to do well.

He is a nice professor but this class is ridiculous. There is a bunch of busy work due every week but most of the material is stuff you don't cover in class so it is typically very frustrating. The class is easy to maintain an A in due to all the extra credit available but you don't get much more besides that out of it.
All I can think about during lecture is "how is it possible that he still teaches at this institution?"  Lectures are horrid, assignments are never put up on time.

analysis.name: Amal Fadlalla
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She gave very vague directions for assignments and would not clarify. Very passive-aggressive over email and in person. She will grade assignments on whether she liked your work or not, and will not provide a rubric. She never teach during class, but requires her students to lead lectures. This was in  AAS 490

Very unclear on all assignments. She is rude when you ask for clarification and acts like you have no reason to be confused despite her vague prompts and directions. I actually had her for AAS 490 and would not recommend.

amal is a horrible teacher. there are no rubrics for assignments, she sends out vague emails then sends rubrics AFTER the fact. she grades arbitrarily & the group paper assignment at the end of the course is RIDICULOUS. readings are long & could be better chosen, she's very disorganized & often comes to class & office hours unprepared.

This was the absolute WORST professor I have ever had. Students teach the entire course, she does absolutely nothing the entire semester. Papers will be graded based on how she would write the paper, not the creative ability of the student or how they interpreted the CONFUSING prompt she provided. Your entire grade is passed on group work as well.

Genuinely the WORST professor I have had. Student lectures entirely run the class, she doesn't even teach! Your grade will be entirely based on group work(she assigns the groups), and if you have a problem with a group member, she will not intervene (even if it is an issue with unequal participation). I do not recommend ANY class taught by her.

analysis.name: Barbara Ericson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This was my first programming class at UMich and definitely a step up from what I was used to. Grading time took a long time; however, it wasn't really an issue for me. A major positive is the extra credit, which gives chances to make up points. Overall, the class is challenging but fair if you put in the effort, and you should get an A.

All her grades are at least 2 weeks late, never on time, and you have to go to office hours to ask anything regarding your assignments. Every question has it's own form you have to fill out. Your emails won't be responded to, and you have to use Piazza to communicate. Her class format is the only good, but the discussion sections are the worst.

Her descriptions of assignments or projects is the worst, she takes 3x as much words to explain the same thing in much simpler contexts. Her TA's delay everything, they're all basically other undergraduate students who simply cannot afford to prioritize just her class over other stuff obviously. God knows why she won't hire GSI's.

Barbara was not a very clear lecturer; however, this class is very dependent on your own studying and review, not so much on lectures. Overall, an unmemorable class but a solid textbook, and you will definitely learn how to code in Python more.

The workload is doable and there were about 2 or 3 exams, about 10 or 11 homeworks, discussion assignments, and 3 projects. The lectures were informative and the in-lecture practices, as well as the assignments they were helpful as well. The class is late on grading and a bit crammed in.

analysis.name: Alicia Romero
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 170 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: idk why ppl hate, i had keane and i would watch her lectures since I thought she made it easier to digest, whoever u have for stats youll be fine. stats is an semi easy but boring subject, do active approach, and check hw and case study with others and youll get an A easily dw

She's a great lecturer and especially helpful in OA and after class. Though STATS250 is an easy class by no means it is an 'easy A' imo. There's homework, MWrite, Labs, xyz... Just keep up with what's going on, try to get full marks on each homework and use office hours, you'll be fine. Lectures are recorded and you can go to any lecturer, dw.

Romero is lowkey overhated. She did make a few conceptual mistakes when teaching lectures, but expressed most things clearly. You can decide if you want attendance, pre-lecture, and post-lecture work to count toward your grade. There are not a lot of study materials provided for the exams (you get 1 practice exam and a concept problem set).

This was my first time taking a Stats class in my entire life, and honestly, the content itself was easy to grasp, but she assumes everyone in the room has prior knowledge. After a few weeks, she toned it down and slowed to a much more manageable pace. She is very approachable, though, and going to office hours is SUPER helpful!

I don't understand the Romero hate. She is a great lecturer, even though the content can be dull. She is very nice and engaging and always willing to help and answer questions. Office hours are completely done with GSIs, though, but they are still very helpful and knowledgeable! I would definitely not skip out on Romero for stats.

analysis.name: Bryan Roby
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Roby is a professor I had the displeasure of ending up with. His grading criteria are incredibly unclear and his approach to teaching is "life doesn't give you a syllabus." His lectures are dependant on information he expects you to learn on your own (that he doesn't tell you about) and there is barely a common theme in the class.

Bryan Roby is an absolute legend. Literally the smartest professor in his field. You will be suprised how much you learn about Judaism in North Africa. I went into the class with no ambition and proceeded to write one of the greatest essays of my life. Please take him if you can, he's so amazing and this was my favorite class ever at Michigan.

Professor Roby is the best non-engineering professor I have had at the University of Michigan. Workload is light, the class is super revolved around participation and engagement which I love. He really cares for the students and he makes you realize that the main goal for this class isn't to get an A but actually learn the Judaic content.
Professor Roby is very understanding and really is just looking for people to engage in class discussion. If you just participate in class you are almost guaranteed an A. Solid class.
One of the best professors I have ever had. Really caring and I really think he is one of many few professors who truly cares for their students and realizes we have lives outside of class.

analysis.name: Michael Burke
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I made a rate my professor account just to write nice things about this guy. If you have an opportunity to take 290 with him TAKE IT!!! He always made himself available for questions, told fun stories about his experience in the industry and he takes time to get to know all of his students.

Professor Burke is a fantastic instructor and provides excellent in-class teaching that correlates to real-world experiences in production. I would highly recommend taking this course with Burke if you are looking for impactful criticism, support, and guidance related to all things writing, editing, and production!

This was my favorite professor of my first year of college, he is so caring and understanding. I went through a very rough time mentally during his class and missed alot of lectures and he still made sure i understood everything we were doing. Love this guy so much

Michael Burke was one of the best professors I have had at UMich. He is the coolest guy and taught us so much about the industry through his own experience and by producing ourselves. There are 2 group projects outside of class, but they generally take only a day each and are super fun. Take his class!!!!!

Best professor I have had at school thus far. Always helpful and available whenever you need it. Understanding when things go wrong. Offers great feedback and teaches the content incredibly. I'd give more than 5 stars if I could.

analysis.name: Megan Bardolph
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bardolph is extremely relaxed, comical, and understanding; her lectures are more socratic, chalkboard-based. She's made me more confident in my ability to critically analyze rhetoric across research studies, classical texts, and modern media. Grading is mostly weighted by 2 essays (with revisions) plus attendance. P.S. you may learn to juggle!

Professor Bardolph is genuinely one of the best professors that the school has to offer. She takes a seemingly mundane and boring class (ENG125), and adds so much complexity and thought into how to develop our rhetoric to gain a better understanding of writing and academic inquiry. Also an extremely sweet lady and clearly cares for her students!

Dr. Bardolph is amazing! She made the lectures interesting and enjoyable. I really enjoyed my time in her class and the things we discussed have helped me a lot. She is very friendly and always willing to talk about literally anything!

Prof Bardolph is so sweet and cares so much about the well-being of her students! She barely gave any work outside of class. The class was not super helpful in improving English skills and focused more on rhetoric which is not what I had expected, but she made it pretty enjoyable. Class is very very easy and not much is missed if you skip lecture.

Very light workload and engaging lectures made her class the highlight of otherwise tough days for me. She assigns work qualitatively with succinct but thoughtful guidelines I found nice. Hands down the perfect FYWR class you could take.

analysis.name: Lesa Begley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Begley is a great professor. Her lectures are informative, and the slides are all posted online. The projects and homework are very easy, and you are given a ton of time on them. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I would still go since the lectures can be entertaining. Overall, excellent professor and class.
Wish I knew why I was honor coded :(. Makes no sense to hand it out when students don't know why and trouble their lives for it to prove they're right and still lose.

This professor wasn't very accessible via the duration of the course despite wielding substantial stakes over final course grades. It's as if potential communication opportunities with them was purposefully limited on their end.
ENGR 101 professors are incredibly committed to their student's success.

analysis.name: Benjamin Mullins
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: No perfect scores in the problem set or exams. On one of my sets, my code worked perfectly and there were no errors; I had points taken off because of ONE indent (GSIs were in on this too). Likes his other job better.

The professor works really hard. But I thought the lecture was a little out-of-date. Some code style and functionality is useless during actual work. In addition, I don't understand why the professor is so stuck on explaining something really easy to understand. He should provide more useful stuff in this course, or it will just be a waste of time

Warning: Lecture Heavy & Test Heavy! He uses buffer Credit Lottery Policy: 3 days will be chosen randomly that will earn buffer credit. Days with fewer overall entries will earn more points (in other words, low attendance means more points for those who show up).

This was one of the most toughest classes because I don't have a CS background. He is very helpful outside of class but office hours were limited to only Fridays for a few hours. GSI was also helpful but you may need to study a lot outside of class. He does rush through the lecture but does have recorded lectures. Work hard and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Tilman Borgers
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are just him making quiet, awkward jokes to himself. His slides are as barren as the Serengeti.  If you don't go to lecture the slides will be even more confusing, but he does post the slides. The assignments are graded way too harshly and the only reason I was ever able to do them correctly was because of the GSIs. He does seem friendly.

Tilman was a great professor for Econ 401. It's a tough class and requires a lot of work, but he provides lots of extra resources to make sure you succeed and wants to see all of his students do well. Very helpful in office hours and responds very quickly to forums posts and emails. I would definitely recommend taking 401 with Tilman.
Without a doubt, the best economics professor I have ever had! Incredibly supportive and always willing to help students grow and improve.

Realizing how good I had it compared to 402 with Cravino.  I thought he was one of the best Econ professors I've had, he explained things concisely and was entertaining in lecture. 401 like most Econ classes is one where you have to work through the problems on your own to understand, but his lectures were  useful and discussion was very much so.

One of the worst experiences of my life, my GSI would grade really tough and when I complained to him he went off on me during office hours. He grades really tough, all you need to know before taking this class is partial derivatives, chain rule, product rule, first and second order condition and you should be fine. He FAILED 30 STUDENTS, UNREAL.

analysis.name: Bethany Kreps
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Mme. Kreps is really nice. I feel her class is an easy way to meet friends.We covered a lot of material . Be prepared to speak french the entire class because that can help dock down your points. Overall, I feel like it was a great intro class and she followed all my SSD accodmations.

I haven't even finished the class yet, but she's definitely my best teacher this semester and probably this year. Super kind, very flexible, caring, and understanding. As long as you try, you'll definitely get a good grade.

I really liked Madame Kreps. I hated French in High School, but I enjoyed this class. I hate participating in class and participation was a part of our grade so I was nervous going in, but she made me feel really comfortable and the class is small so it's not that bad. She was a pretty nice grader and gave us a lot of feedback on our work.

Professor Kreps was an extremely kind and understanding professor! She was easy to understand and very approachable, so oral exams and asking questions weren't as scary as I thought they would be. Participation wasn't as difficult as I expected either since the class was small and Professor Kreps made the environment comfortable.

I would highly recommend people take Mme. Kreps classes! She was one of my favorite profs here so far, she kept the class stress-free, and I never felt nervous to participate or afraid to make mistakes. She's very kind and if you participate in class you should do really well

analysis.name: Cynthia Gabriel
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are dense and she moves through slides so quickly it is impossible to write everything down. This is inconvenient because the tests she assigns require you to remember specific statistics discussed in lecture. The final project is also difficult because of the parameters she sets for your sources which makes them almost impossible to find.

This course was extremely difficult for an introductory, elective course. The quizzes were too specific and expected you to remember everything we went over in each 2 hour lecture. The readings are also extremely questionable in their scholarly validity. The sources she asks us to provide are nearly impossible to find under the parameters she sets.

Places very strict expectations on students but does not follow them herself. She expects proper academic sources no older than 10 years and based in the US yet gives us Tumblr posts as class reading material. She expects perfect writing on all assignments and no errors in our citations yet makes grammatical errors on the quizzes she writes. Awful

Very test heavy, test questions are super specific and at times even after taking the quiz you will still be unsure of the answers after reviewing the articles. Questions on exams about lecture are very tricky, as all could be true, just not specifically said during the lecture.

WGS220 expectations are ridiculous. Though interesting, it was not worth the STRESS nor the GPA hit from the grading that is intensely nitty-gritty. Dr. Gabriel is a smart woman, however the way she structures this course feels almost mean. Nothing is easy about the work that's expected, and half of the assignments/quizzes felt set up for failure.

analysis.name: Mark Brehob
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 97 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: In my own view, this lecturer simple does not know the material at all. He is not clear in his presentation of the material and is very unhelpful and negative with respect to students' academic objectives.
He speaks extremely fast. He frequently jumps between different points but always fails to mention the connections. He is helpful during office hours and caring though.

Surprised by some of the negative reviews here, especially regarding insensitivity. I'm black and I've never felt any sort of racism from Brehob. He's an incredible lecturer. He's hilarious, and he knows his stuff. He's got great OH, and he really cares about his students. A top-tier professor.

Amazing kind and respectful teacher. The best teacher I have interacted with at umich in general, he is so sweet kind and respectful. I have never met a teacher like him and honestly I am so happy I took it with him during this semester and not beaumont even though I know he's also good. Extremley underrated and amazing professor! Take him!!
I cannot understand what his accent. Maybe it's too difficult for an international student. His tone makes me wanna sleep too.

analysis.name: Christian Fong
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Best professor I have had at Michigan. Highly recommend taking his class. If you pay attention and try (e.g., go to office hours), you will do well. It is obvious that he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. If you are even considering this for any reason, take it!!!!!!

Prof. Fong was one of the best professors I've ever had. There were engaging lectures, and the class was very interesting. The assignments are difficult, and it's definitely not an easy A, but Prof. Fong will set you up for success in this class and is more than willing to help you in any of your future endeavors.

This class was really amazing and challenging at the same time. The sections were fantastic and fun! The memos at times were frustrating, but if you ask questions and genuinely respond to the prompt, you will get an A. It's a grind, but really worth taking, but super career-oriented though.

Very career-oriented class. If you don't want to work on the Hill, I don't recommend this class. Prof Fong is knowledgeable and interesting, but his grading criteria is unclear and definitely has a learning curve to it. If you master the memos, it isn't hard to get an A.

Lectures are fantastic but discussions involve some of the most confusing games that involve manipulating and lying to other classmates to better your own grade. While they're technically relevant to lectures, they don't really help to understand the material.

analysis.name: James Casey Jr.
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Casey was nice, accessible, and explained concepts clearly. However, he tended to misspeak sometimes which made things confusing. His memorization questions on exams were simple, but his application questions were incredibly difficult. They felt beyond the scope of this course, but he was fair in removing them/giving partial credit.

He is definitely better than Haenfler when it comes to explaining material. I like the way he lectures. The final exam was very difficult. 80 questions with intense application-based questions that required a lot of thinking outside of what we learned in class. 4th exam had a lot of spelling errors and didn't look like it was revised.

This class is really hard for some reason. Exams often ask unfair questions that contradict what we learned in class. He is pretty good with dropping questions/giving partial credit. However, the time I spend studying for the class is not representative in the grading at all.

Good lecturer. The class is content heavy so the exams are difficult. You get extra credit from submitting questions on piazza. Has ocassional choose all that apply questions that are difficult. Starts class right at the start time with an iclicker question. iclicker is graded. Class has case studies done in groups before every exam.

I don't really get the hype. I just feel like everything is all over the place when he lectures and stuff is smushed together. Some of the exam questions make no sense it's mind boggling. I sense a lack of care too when it comes to going over stuff that's heavy on the exam.

analysis.name: Colleen Van Lent
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: (SI 101 used to be called 106) Colleen is the best and cares about her students. shes reasonable, understanding and would always give extensions on our assignments. Readings are helpful since lectures can be fast but many did fine without. 3 exams, 1 makeup date, 1 final project(group or alone), 3 'HWs', weekly quizzes and lecture activities(easy).

Colleen is an extremely kind professor, she always makes sure no one is confused and questions are answered. As far as teaching in class, she assumes you know a lot so definitely stay on top of readings if you actually want to understand what she is saying. She offers a lot of extra credit at the end of the semester so your grade will be ok.

Several extra credit opportunities. If you do well on exam 1 and 2 and do the rest of your assignments, you can take a 0/100 on exam 3 and still get an A (what I did). She's super nice and caring. Amazing prof. Would take again.

Course could be more organized, but overall it's not that bad. You might have to work a bit harder for a few assignments, but if you're a CS major taking it as an elective (like me), the workload should be much lower than what you're used to. Colleen and the GSIs are nice and try their best to help out too.

This class is so stupid, the auto grader is so stupid. There are so many ways to write the CSS to get the same effect but the professor and GSIs just choose to use the auto grader which is so rigid and it doesn't make sense at all! Why can't you just grade people's homework by LOOKING INTO THEIR CODE?!

analysis.name: Chris Proulx
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 277 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Pretty much going to echo the feedback here: 401 is a challenging class and Proulx's lectures do little to help. Some people think he's funny but to me he just comes off as pretty rude and his slides will do nothing to help you prepare for the exam in the class. Your best resources in this class are your GSIs/discussion sections and YouTube videos.
Is unclear and is rude to students when they ask questions. Someone asked a question in lecture as to how he got a certain answer and he responded "like I just did."

The rabbit's lectures are quite theoretical indeed, and I loved all his anecdotes and humor. However, his lectures do little to prepare you for the exam. Save your time - don't use the textbook at all. I survived this class by networking with others who were able to explain problems. Look at the workbook for sure, some questions come from there.

Don't take 401 with Proulx if you have a choice. He barely gives examples, and when he does, they are far from what's on his tests. To make matters worse, his recommended textbook is useless. It is the first textbook I have seen without common examples. I really hoped the textbook would help prepare me for tests but it's as useless as the lectures.

I want to be fair. Proulx can be funny and he can really helpful during office hours. But I can't deny the fact that this class is so stupidly tough because he makes it so. There's absolutely no need to blow through material so quickly while teaching proofs and other things that just needlessly complicate material. 401 shouldn't be bad, but it is.

analysis.name: Henry Cowles
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great professor. He really cares about his students and I feel like I learned a lot. His lectures are really interesting so you should show up. Also super cute and kinda jacked hmu Henry

This guy is great. His classes are very interesting, and he is a great person to chat with in office hours. It's clear that he genuinely cares about his students and his teaching philosophy is very purely academic, with a strong emphasis on learning for it's own sake. Always a joy to go to his class, and I'm excited to take him again!

He's super nice and funny in lecture, you can really tell he loves teaching this subject. His lectures are organized well, but he doesn't really put words on the slides, so notes definitely need to be taken throughout lecture, because the powerpoints will tell you nothing. Would take again, he was amazing!

This class was so easy and Dr. Cowles' lectures were super interesting. There were 2 readings/week that were probably around 40ish pages total. 3 papers, the longest of which is 1500 words. Once a week we did collaborations in lecture, and I really enjoyed these- these mostly involved designing a product or an ad related to our topic for the week.

Professor Cowles is amazing. He truly cares about his students and his lectures are fascinating. He does lecture with little words on the slides, so it's important to listen, but he really is very knowledgeable. Would 100% take this class again!

analysis.name: Henry Chai
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Very chill guy, makes jokes at lecture. Gives a bunch of practice problems during lecture to help students practice.
Very engaging lectures; professor genuinely cares about his students. Class is very manageable if practice problems are done without cheating.
Guy is engaging and knows what he is talking about and also super chill

analysis.name: Edward Chang
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 181 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Chang was awesome! He made this big 250+ class an open discussion course. Five exams, no papers or projects, and easy extra credit offered! 11 five question pop quizzes and tells you what section to study! Must read the textbook to do well on exams, but they're fair. Doesn't use CTools (no notes posted) and no electronics in class. Great class!

He believes that he is a liberal arts teacher, but does not teach in a progressive and meaningful way. He hosts lectures that give information pertaining to his childhood and life experiences, but dont help in the understanding or learning of content. His tests are extremely difficult and have nothing to do with what he teaches. He wasted my time.

Professor Chang is a great lecturer.  He acts tough, but he's a nice guy.  Gave out a fair amount of extra credit.  Must attend class and read the book to get an A.  Gives a half a point for speaking in class, and does want to hear from his students.  Take advantage of it. I missed an A- by a single point because I didn't speak two more times.

Dr. Chang is a good lecturer who told interesting stories about his work experience. There is a big emphasis on the textbook. I sometimes felt like we were not tested on the main concepts, but rather, on random details from both the textbook and lecture. Going to class and reading the textbook are both very important for success in the class.

For people who want to take his class just be aware that nothing is online everything is in person. no laptops are allowed in the class or phones and he will call you out if you go on your phone. doesn't use canvas or anything he hands out exam grades in lecture. you have no resources other then lecture and discussion and office hours.

analysis.name: Carly Nowicki
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: i ain't even out of her class yet and im already so sick of these papers. labs aren't hard at all, its the follow-up assignments that'll kill you. plus its wild that your grade is determined basically by your exams, since lab attendance doesn't count for much. shes also incredibly passive aggressive and her lectures feel like shes yelling at you.

Labs were a little tedious and were very dependent on your GSI (shoutout to my goat Kai).

If you've ever wanted to relive high school, this is the class. She talks to everyone like we're 15, polite yet condescending, and exams are so vague, it's just about decoding her wording. There are exams instead of lab practicals and way too many random assignments for a LAB course. Good luck, being a required class,sadly, there's no escaping her.

Her lectures really are not terrible, but I do not agree with the way that the class is structured at all. Nowicki requires us to stay in lab all 3 hours, regardless of productivity, and to be entirely honest--is not the friendliest. Honestly probably would take again if was the only choice, but def not on my own accord.

This class may seem easy, but the tests are confusing and full of trick questions. I read every recommended textbook section and still struggled. The content isn't hard, but the way it's assessed is unfair. Nowicki often didn't know answers to her own questions and made frequent mistakes in lectures and office hours.

analysis.name: Douglas Northrop
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Northrop is a nice guy but I wouldn't recommend his class. I took this class during a half-term and the amount of material covered was just too much for 6 weeks. He's so nice and so smart. You can tell he really cares about history and teaching. But the workload is insane. Sometimes 200 pages of reading PER CLASS (2 classes/week). Readings are dense and difficult. 2 big projects, both really hard. Doesn't make sense that this is 3 credit class. Still enjoyed him and this class a lot though.

Generally very nice, very smart, and very knowledgable about topics. He was a pretty fair grader, but assigned a LOT of work - dense, difficult reading of around 100 pages + big essays. Felt like it should be a 4 credit class given that I had the most work in this course vs my other 4 credit courses. Really liked him as a teacher though.

Northrop is easily the WORST professor I have had at umich. His lectures are incredibly boring, his slides only have pictures and do not help to learn the content, he requires an awful amount of reading, and his exams are ridiculous. He spent most of the time talking about Colonial CA, but his exam questions are primarily about pre-Colonial CA.

This is specifically for his online classes. Expect to be graded as if you are writing essays as a historian and your document is being professionally peer-reviewed. His essay prompts are extremely vague (worst part of the class IMO). Also, he assumes everyone is cheating during online exams and makes his exams much much harder.

analysis.name: Charles Severance
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload

review_highlights.comment: He is one of the best Teacher I have seen and one best mentor. May Gol always keep him happy

Took it thinking I would learn SQL/db design, but not the case. Homeworks were easy but could be time consuming. Midterm and final were a breeze. Take if you need 3 CHs

He knows what he talks about. I enjoyed being able to work on the homework tutorials on my own time after I was finished with other prioritized homework. I learned a lot. SI 504 comes in clutch since we use the terminal a lot as well.

I took the Python classes on Amazon/video. When i started I knew absolutly nothing about programing and or computers, I was totaly green, but with his lectures has made it so easy that i keep wondering where was I yesterday. Kudos ! an exceptional teacher, Humble and to the point. Thank you. i'm going to continue with the rest of his classes too.

hey! i am one of the student who is taking coursera classes. the series on python is amazing and the best i have seen so far! awesome knowing this class and thank you a lot for providing us the opportunity to learn online, especially for those of us who do not have privilege to pursue a formal computer class  Thank you again!!

analysis.name: Mitchell Dudley
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dudley is one of the best professors I've had at the University of Michigan. He is super enthusiastic about economics and wants his students to succeed. Tests are fair; he does not test anything not covered in lecture. Workload was light, but you learn a lot. He is also generous enough to offer extra credit; 55% of the class got an A this semester!

Not my favorite... Lectures were never engaging and I found his teaching style hard to follow. Exams were not impossible, but definitely not easy. He has very high expectations for his students and can be really persnickety. Just always kind of doing too much. Discussion sections are optional as well, which is nice.

The 5 quiz format is wayyy more difficult than the other econ 101 classes and I can't be convinced otherwise. Content is much more difficult on quizzes than what is gone over in the lectures and discussions. He will try to trick you on the quizzes. Writing fellows grade everything and will take points off whenever possible. I enjoyed his dialogues.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH DUDLEY!!!! It is not his usual teaching assignment, and he made it clear to us day one that he would not be taking our class seriously. Expected to memorize long lists of random words for the three exams that made up final grade. No practice work given ever, so no homework, but also no non-lecture way to learn content.

This might be one of the worst classes I have ever taken at Michigan. Beware of the hype because you will regret taking this course with Professor dudley. To start out with Professor dudleys lectures are extremely dumbed down and not helpful for tests. GSI is not even fluent in English and makes no sense. You are graded by 19 year olds. Avoid.

analysis.name: Ronald Dreslinski
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The course was co-taught by three professors. Ron is great among them. He tries to give clear explanations. He often gives the students the chance to practice by themselves and he will go around to discuss the questions with them. A reliable instructor for the course.
Literally made me want to go into an embedded systems career

First non-A I've gotten in college, but still learned more than I have in any other class. Dr. Dreslinski is an awesome professor - super understanding, clear lectures, and answers every question that comes his way. As a first-generation student, he's also an amazing mentor. A real gem in the EECS department, grateful to had him as a professor!
Ron is one of the few professors who actually care if his students learn. Would take a class with him any day.
He was prepared for lectures, and explained concepts well. He's also approachable which is a big, big plus in the EECS department. Gonna miss him, and hope he keeps up the good work.

analysis.name: Diane Spillane

The only professor at umich I truly dislike. The class environment was not supportive or encouraging and honestly made me feel uncomfortable and not supported. Honestly one of the worst professors I've had. She constantly put down students, spoke in a condescending tone, and showed no effort to understand different perspectives. Instead of creating an encouraging learning environment, she made class stressful and unproductive.

I knew from the first day of class that she was going to be horrible; I am not looking forward to having her for the semester. She made it explicitly clear that an A is exceptional work, even though it is an introductory class for English. So sad.

Super nice teacher and not a lot of work. I did a hybrid class which made it even more chill, fridays always on zoom and sometimes cancelled. Totally recommend for non-english majors who need a FYWR. One of my favorite teachers definitely take her class!!

Contrary to what everyone's saying, she's a great person but a horrible professor to have for an introductory to English class. Avoid her unless you have a passion for writing, too much work.

analysis.name: Jeff Dunworth
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: OH YEAH!!! Professor Dunworth is the greatest professor who ever lived who isn't not a Math 285 instructor. useless professor who did not lecture at all during class. every time during class, he just gives out practice problems for you to do in groups and assumed that everyone understood everything from reading the textbook. however, none of the groups knew what they were doing. do not do his class

He will, at his own whims, add or drop questions on homework or midterms (made a test much longer than past years to drop avg by 10%). He wants you to fail while pretending he's there to help, making it more difficult for you to succeed at every turn possible.

Sure, maybe Dunworth a great professor as people say. But for the semesters when you're left with him as the course coordinator, he and MATH215 fail miserably. You're stuck with a lecturer that you can barely understand, a terrible lab GSI, and ridiculous HW. MATH215 was the most poorly taught class I've taken in both high school and college.

I was about to get an A, but suddenly Dunworth crashlanded and taught me how to model brainrot with nonlinear PDEs. I failed my exam and got a D just like everyone.
I confronted him in OH and he said:
“It's not about the tenure.. it's about sending a message. Everything curves!” 
before vanishing into thin air. 
Noone is Dunworthy of his brilliance

Take a different professor if you're interested in actually learning about writing, craft, analysis, etc. Nice guy and good facilitator with a pretty mild workload, but he's a poor teacher.
David is such a nice and understanding guy. It's kind of impossible to dislike him even if you don't like his teaching style. Super chill guy, super chill class. Definitely would recommend
David was a super cool guy overall and the class was interesting.  He did grade my papers kinda tough, but was always willing to meet in or outside of office hours.

Ward was really enthusiastic and was a great choice for my FYWR. Be aware that the classes can get redundant and annoying but he tries to make it interesting. I really have some more intense choice words for this guy but basically he's gonna make things really hard and then act like it was super straight forward. He is a very nice guy! Had a little bit of a difficult time making exams short enough to comfortably complete in the 50min class period (because the class used to be 1.5 hours). However, he seemed to be very rectifying that. Discussions are not bad--in fact very easy.

Duda is the most boring lecturer I've had at Michigan. He drones on about snails, is terrible at answering questions, and randomly cancels his office hours. The class is an easy A, but is not very satisfying. Read the textbook bc you won't learn anything from his lectures. Tests heavily based off of emphasis in lectures. Don't memorize equations.

Endi was the worst professor I have ever had. Never in my academic career have I had an altercation with a professor, but Endi's borderline and sometimes highly offensive remarks, passive aggressive judgement and blatant feedback about not only you as a person but your work has people running out the door before he comes in after hours.

Endi Poskovic made countless passive aggressive remarks towards me and other students. Generally, professors at University of Michigan are respectable and reasonable. However, Endi is an exception. Expect to sit through all his useless life stories and offensive comments on you. This Boomer class is just him reminiscing about ‘days before tiktok' while dismissing student work that isn't immediately connected to his definition of "art". One of my biggest regrets of my college career was not taking advantage of Henriettes willingness to help. If you show her that you want to do well, she will make sure you do well. Best professor in the physics dept for sure!

Professor Elvang is awesome! She's super enthusiastic and cares a lot about her students. She's super nice, willing to help and gives great lectures. One thing that I want all people to know about Henriette is that she CARES about whether you learn the content or not. That makes a big difference. She is a very nice and kind teacher, lenient on giving hw extensions because she wants to make sure we all learn things from the assignments. All around excellent professor. The course leaned a little bit heavier on the more introductory topics this semester, but there is nothing inherently wrong with that. Professor B was a very straightforward lecturer in 215 last semester. He was approachable and patient with my silly questions at office hours.

Well, good luck if you MUST take her.

Caldwell is the man. He makes Economics interesting and likes to joke with his classes. Dr. Vandenbossche is one of my favorite professors at U of M. She was so kind and supportive, and she truly wants the best for her students. She kept classes interesting and made me want to pursue writing throughout my college career.

analysis.name: Michael Weiss

Would HIGHLY recommend him for any math class

Loved his class. He gave good commentary on the material, provided videos to watch outside of class, and I think went more in depth than his peers. He's also very nice.

Genetics is a difficult class, and Dr. Zhang was not very good at explaining concepts. It sometimes felt like he couldn't explain certain questions, and he would sometimes get the questions wrong in class. Tests were also very difficult!

analysis.name: Retika Adhikari

If you like being anxious about your grades, not knowing what is expected of you on every assignment, and ending up with lower grades with no explanation, Professor Adhikari is perfect for you. Despite asking for criteria, she continues to grade based on "how she wants it written". If you think this is going to be an easy A then don't take this professor.

ahn is by far an amazing prof, makes stats interesting with fun pop culture references and is just a cool, jolly guy

I do like them apples, Aaron!

Professor Arthur is one of my favorite professors so far. Very friendly and funny. Only downside about this class is having to do 5 projects (first 2 are easy but the last 3 can be time consuming and difficult)  but besides that this class is pretty easy if you pay attention.

analysis.name: Anne Axel

She's very knowledgeable and helpful, always willing to go the extra mile if you are too. She does rely heavily on the reading material though.
Easy for a nat sci credit. She genuinely cares about the students and really tries to make class interesting.

Yeah. I did not like the topic of this class, it sounded interesting but I was BORED the entire semester. People spend more time on the internet then they do paying attention. He is a nice guy and very passionate!

Super kind and caring but a lot of reading. Only a few short essays and two group projects throughout the semester, but there are usually hefty readings + reading responses every week. Would totally recommend for an easyish humanities credit, but be prepared to read and participate.

The most caring professor at UM! Loved taking her class. Had one final project we worked on throughout the semester, and learned so so much, definitely recommend taking amcult 204 with her if you can.
The nicest Professor you will ever have! She is so relatable and gets what her students have on their plates. Her lectures are really interesting, and I learned so much in her class!

THE worst professor I've encountered at U-M in 4 years. Abrasive and unfortunately his lectures seem like an afterthought

It's been almost three weeks since the final paper was due, and he still hasn't put in a final grade. Canceled class a lot and didn't really ever teach, mostly just talked at us. Easy class though... I guess. I wouldn't recommend

There are many things I'd like to say about Professor Awkward. The class itself was an easy A, but that was it's only perk.

analysis.name: Anna Attie

Anna is a great professor and truly cares about her students. English 125 was not a course that I was excited to take but I am very happy that I took it with her. She is very flexible with deadlines and finds great ways to get her teaching through to the students.
Great professor and so easy to talk to about anything! I would love to take this class again anytime

analysis.name: Sarah Aton
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I've never been put to sleep by a lecturer so quickly. She provides no online resources and is next to useless as an instructor. Avoid her at all costs, she will make you wish you had your "bad" professors back. Stick to research, Sarah. Teaching isn't for you.

Prof Aton is a great lecturer and professor. She clearly goes over what students need to learn, and creates concise slides. Super accessible after class or in office hours, and very patient with students learning hard material. I've definitely benefitted from taking this class with Dr. Aton.

Extremely difficult to follow in lecture, put very little information on her slides and then would talk extremely quickly and never repeat any of the important information. I always had to review at least a third of the lectures on blue review to catch the information I had missed.

Absolute gem of a class to take during COVID. She was very understanding and work load was VERY manageable. I watched all lectures the weekend before the exam and pulled an A+. The extra credit offered in this class is absolutely BONKERS (50 test points!) so you can essentially fail a test and still end with a 100% in the class. Highly Recommend!!!

Dr. Aton is a great lecturer, and her lectures are a really great resource. That being said, her exams were significantly harder than the professor for the other half of this course (Dr. Duan) in my opinion. Her exams pull from the lectures, but they require a lot more thought and synthesis. Application of the lecture material, not regurgitation.

Wait for a better prof for 484
EECS 484 with Prakash is a miserable experience. Projects: awful. Homework: overcomplicated. Exams: out of left field.

A lot of the material covered in lecture is useful in general, but the real helpful tips, tricks, and solid review of exam material happens in lecture. Prof. Prakash generally has a pretty good idea of what's going on in class, but was sometimes unable to answer difficult questions to student satisfaction. Slides were sometimes poorly prepared.

He did a good job explaining things during lectures. Homework and projects are at another level of difficulty. You have to do some research on your own in order to finish them. Autograders for the first two projects are awful (no feedback). Exams are the most horrific thing, if you can get half of questions right, you are in good shape.

It's a given that he's not as good as Chen, but now that Chen is no longer teaching 482, he's all we have.  A decent professor who didn't seem to live up to the horrible billing others gave him, but not amazing by any means.  Was helpful in showing us why we were failing the autograder a few times, but wasn't overly helpful

She's very personable and is clear in lecture, willing to go over concepts again if they seem to be tricky. She's the reason I'm doing well in the class.

Christina was a fantastic GSI. By far, she was the best teacher I had for my first semester. She is extremelly caring and considerate. I was lucky to have her, and really think I would have done worse w/o h

Christina is a very smart, caring young woman. She will take the time to remember your name and call on you using your name, even in a huge classroom. She knows exactly what she is teaching and will explain it to you if you need help. She allows the students to solve the problems out in front of the class so we can better grasp the material.
Christina was the best math teacher I have ever had. She was so helpful (go to office hours). Even when I wasn't in her class, she would help me with math. There isn't enough good things I can say!

Not a good prof.

Not a good teahcer!He knows a lot but he just doesn't know how to teach.His English is really bad,never asks students if we could catch up.Even worse,he is not welcoming students during his office hour,says he can only have three students in his office at a time. She puts on this incredibly nice persona but deep down she is feeding on our tears. Homework is only difficult because it wasn't covered and is poorly worded. Ella Atkins is a sorry excuse for a teacher. She clearly has no regard for her students or for their learning. Her project are ridiculously time consuming for the sake of being time consuming.

review_highlights.comment: Michal teaches with a sense of humanity which is humbling. I appreciate her teaching style and would take the class again. She involves a field trip near the beginning of the semester.

For a one credit class it was a very heavy workload. There were a few lectures but they were not beneficial. Good at responding to emails quickly. Very tough grader. Not worth the time.
This is the second class I've taken with this professor. Easy grader, but she doesn't put in a lot of work.

Dr. Michal is so great! Her class is also super easy (no exams!). Weekly assignments but all manageable. Her lectures are also engaging, since she includes relatable videos from movies/tv shows and demos that get the class involved. There is a group project at the end, but nothing difficult. She's also a sweetheart, loved her and her class!

weekly discussion quizzes were pretty easy, and exams which were held online came mostly from the slides and examples from lecture. The readings posted from canvas were extremely long. Make sure not to fall behind on lecture material, and fill out the study guide with lecture notes and whatever is from the readings. Not an Easy A, but very doable.

No one goes to class because he is THE WORST professor I have ever had. Avoid him at all costs if you want to actually learn something.

This course is absolutely miserable. Attending lectures is useless. He uses nothing but powerpoints which make you fall asleep. He doesn't care about the course, or what you think. He doesn't seem to care about teaching in general, very disorganized. Avoid him like the plague.

analysis.name: Audrey Becker
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: RCDRAMA 102 is an introductory improv class. This class taught me all about improv, and the professor encouraged me to step up and participate in many games.

This was an improv games class open to rc and non rc students. Truly such a great experience and Dr. Audrey made this class so fun. Definitely take a class with her - she cares so much about her students and has a wonderfully positive attitude that makes everyone feel welcome!

I took her pilot class and I didn't enjoy it as much as I thought I would, but she was fine. Personally, I don't get along well with her teaching style, but I think overall she's a passionate and great professor.

Planned a lot of helpful projects and activities that were engaging and truly helped with learning about theatre and acting. Gave great feedback about performances and encouraged a community space so it never felt awkward performing in front of peers. There was a lot of reading, but the plays were interesting and engaging to dive into as an actor.

I've never met anyone with more knowledge of Early Modern drama than Audrey Becker. Her passion for the topic shows and she finds different ways for everyone to connect with the material. She pushes you to improve as a student, writer, and performer, and she can adapt her critique based on your experience in theater performance.

analysis.name: Micah Auerback
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The workload is absurd.1500+ pages of reading, 500 word essay due EVERY SUNDAY & TUESDAY, multiple presentations & a midterm/final that total 5000+ words. No useful writing feedback & grades everything the last week. His expectations for the effort students should put into a 3 credit INTRO ELECTIVE are severely out of touch.

Weekly essays and readings that are pretty heavy, refusal to give any resources outside of lectures, and the minimum for an A is a 95 for an INTRODUCTORY class! Calls people out for having technology in class and forces students to write handwritten notes. We had one major quiz besides the pop quizzes, and that was on resources OUTSIDE of lectures.

Dense readings used to write weekly papers. In lecture, he would say non-english words in and overly accentuated accent that is uncomfortable. Quizzes were on materials that had to be learned outside of class. Multiple choice on exams were very specific and subjective and he did not provide any resources to practice, even when asked.
He gives a lot of work for an intro to asian studies course. If you do all of it you'll be fine but don't do this class with him if you don't want to do a lot of work.

For an introductory class, the grading scale felt unreasonable (95% for an A). Weekly papers are short + lectures elaborated on the readings so you could get away with skimming most of the readings. No tech, but in class notes don't really help since the midterm + final + essays were based on terms in his study guide (remember ~200 terms per exam).

If you have the choice to take Italian with any prof, it should be him, hands down the best prof I've had at all of UMich
Loved him so funny and I have learned so much italian. Best teacher I have had at Umich by far
He's only nice if he likes you.

Very funny professor. The class is fairly easy as long as you take/study notes.  He highly encourages vocal practice which is great.  The only problem I had was that half the time, I couldn't even understand what he was saying.  His accent is just thick enough to where you have to really pay attention to what he means, or else you will get lost.

review_highlights.comment: she is so knowledgeable it is almost intimidating but she is so nice that it cancels out! she is very eager and open any and every question, and is very forgiving and generous on exams. sometimes a lot of homework, but nothing unmanageable. i didn't really care for linguistics until this class and did find it much more intriguing because of aull!

Many supports and insight and I recommend her class for anyone who want a class more than a FYWR. She make me interested in linguistics even I am not good at English

Mind blowing class!! Dr. Aull does a great job of breaking down everything you've ever learned about English in high school and reformatting your thinking to be more progressive and accurate in the writing world. Makes strong connections w/ her students too. 10/10 professor!!

Dr Aull is an amazing teacher! Definitely the most difficult class I took, but totally worth it! Might end up with a B or C, but the insight and writing skills you acquire are invaluable. I took English 305 as a three-hour course. I would normally have trouble focusing, but Dr. Aull's lectures were so engaging that I never had any difficulty. She's extremely articulate and clearly very passionate. She would always take time to thoughtfully answer every question, and you could tell she values her students' opinions. Take her classes!

review_highlights.comment: I had professor Ayotte for FR231 and 232, although there is lots of homework and stuff, you can tell she cares and wants you to succeed in the class.
