Good prof. but get ready to not get credit for effort

Dr. Bird was a great professor and knows makes lectures fun because of how much knowledge she has on all the content. Gradecraft class so you get to pick what assignments you do. There are 6 exams but as long as you get above a 60% on all of them and attend every class you can get an A+.

analysis.name: Julie Biteen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Biteen is a great professor. She is clearly very passionate about what she's teaching, and she makes pchem concepts much more digestible and easier to understand. She also walks through problems with you and is great to talk to. However, personally, I found some of her lectures to be boring, but that might be due to the material itself.
Biteen is the best! She structures her lectures and the discussions so well, you cannot help but do great! She is really funny and really loves her students. Could not recommend her more highly!

She's new to U of M, but she seems to know her stuff. She goes through the basic chem slides all the other teachers go through as well. She was very nice and is willing to answer questions. iClicker attendance is recommended since they can give you an extra 4% boost in the class. Exams are actually pretty  hard though since she doesn't write them.

Very sweet and caring. She goes at a pretty reasonable pace and is very open to helping people with questions so the lectures and iClickers were fairly easy for me (I had some previous experience with chem honors in high school). The tests are a little challenging though and aren't curved.

She's kind and will answer all of your questions. She occasionally makes no sense and often confuses her words, but if you point it out or go to her office hours, she clarifies. Very sweet and caring, makes cute little jokes here and there.

analysis.name: Bing Zhou
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Pay close attention to what is covered in the review sessions because that is what will be on the exams. Lectures are not particularly insightful. Instructor did not recognize student difficulty with the material. Beware of homework sets they are often long and painful. If you can take the course with someone else do so. Your grade will thank you.

Worst class I have ever taken by far, 100% sure that any grad student would've done better. She read straight off slides for lecture, which were just screenshots from the solution manual. Only 5 people out of 30 were attending lecture after the first month, and every time you asked a question in office hours she would berate you. umich pls fire.

Professor Zhou was truly one of the worst professors that I have had at this school.  She expects everything to make sense the first time around and is very condescending in her explanations.  I was a solid A- average honors physics student going into this class, but completely bombed this course.  Definitely avoid her and try to get someone else.

Bing Zhou is very smart, but not a good lecturer. Her lectures skip over parts that would help student understanding and are scattered. She almost always does not understand students questions and makes mistakes when writing equations that often lead to confusing notes. Read the book, and good luck. If you can, wait for someone else to teach it.

The lectures are just Professor Zhou reading off a slideshow that they opened on Canvas. The homeworks are just book problems. She never walks through problems on a white/blackboard, only talks through them on the slides. I would never take a class with this professor again.

analysis.name: David Blaauw
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: the average for the exam was a 45 and there was 0 circuits involved it was all random fun fact questions on circuits and it was nothing like the TWOOOOO practice questions released like why are we getting set up for failure. why are there 0 good learning materials?

Blaauw is very knowledgeable and a good professor, but the organization + administrative aspects of his courses make it difficult to recommend. He only taught during the final ~4 weeks of the semester. The class was primarily led by GSIs who did their best. Additionally, his exams are extremely difficult, with class averages often below 50%.
Labs are incoherent and completely different from lectures and exam content is NOWHERE to be found it just appears on the exam somehow
Why does the exams have word for word questions from some random fabrication process mentioned for 2 seconds in lecture 1?
The Gsis ran the class he disappeared after day 1 unfortunately otherwise he wouldve been a great teacher :(.

analysis.name: Hoyt Bleakley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: For first few months of the semester, he had a high expectation from upper-level students so he explained the concept with extra details. This obviously confused the students but he simplified things at the end. I went to his office hour every week and got help for the problem set and understanding the concept. Exams are similar to problem sets.

I would genuinely never take 461. Ever. Actively googling "how to late drop a class". All written on a chalkboard. Very disorganized flow of ideas. Unsure of expectations. Lecture recordings are recorded but not made public because why would he make resources available to his students? Must request recordings when absent. No late homework allowed.

This guy is a nice person and all, he does care about the students and tries to give feedback if you ask for it. HOWEVER getting any type of straight answer out of him is like pulling teeth. I have to ask him the same question at least 2 times to get a clear response. Some of the content is really confusing, and he doesn't do his best to help you.

He doesn't seem to prepare for lecture and mandates a lot of assumed knowledge that is closer to a graduate level than undergraduate. If you are not excellent at the modeling side of economics avoid his course.

This class is confusing. He doesn't post lectures or slides online or in an organized manner. His lectures are unclear and uninteresting. Attendance isn't required, but most of the lecture is just him writing on the board, so you won't know what he talked about if you miss class. He's unclear about grading and expectations. Kind of pointless class.

analysis.name: Elliot Blackstone
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Waited until I graduated to make this judgement: Officially THE WORST Professor I have had.Simply put: Unwilling and unable to help one improve, unclear grading, memorization-based learning, dismissive, purely exam-based course grade, homework dissimilar to exams, does not explain concepts rather write definitions on board. Doesn't belong at UMich.

Prof Elliot only writing what is on the book during the lecture. It feels like there is nothing different between learning by yourself at home and listening the lecture. Anyways, the teaching skills is just awful.

Lectures were copied straight from the textbook, but example problems only covered the basics of the topics. Harsh grader on exams, and had poor explanations for grading. Explanations in class were vague, and I understood concepts better after teaching myself them.

Dr. Blackstone was a great professor—he explained everything clearly, graded fairly, and was always there to help with questions. He is sometimes a little bit blunt, but it's kind of funny. Great professor but not an easy class.

Fell far below the general standard of honors math. All exams (80% of our grade!) regurgitated problems from the textbook; studying became memorizing 100+ problems rather than LEARNING & ENJOYING math. Lectures copied from textbook. I started doing SO MUCH better (D -> A) once I started teaching myself from the textbook instead of going to class.

analysis.name: Bill Gehring
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 81 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I absolutely loved Dr. Gehring and his genuine care for each and every student. The interesting material covered in lecture was underscored by his passion for the subject. Exams are fair if you pay attention in lecture and review the study guide. I highly recommend 240 but take any class you can with Dr. Gehring, you won't regret it.

Bill was a great professor during the summer semester. He truly cared for his students and you could tell it too. I wasn't the best student due mental health issues, Bill was willing to take actions to get you where you should be. I've never had a more awesome professor at my time here in Michigan.

Bill Gehring is an amazing professor who clearly cares about the course and students. Only thing I will say is that the demos in class do come in the exam so participate and don't brush them off. Exams do require a lot of studying but aren't impossible. He also encourages AI and includes assignments that teach us about it. Great for BS credit.

He is so sweet and is such a good lecturer. He makes the content understable, even when it can be confusing like parts of the brain. The exams are really straightforward and he does curve them to help everyone out. He wants to get to know you so I recommend office hours or at least emailing him, he wants to hear from you!

Gehring is THE BEST PROFESSOR IVE HAD at uofm! His psych 240 taught me how to actually study and I learned so much in the class despite it being online and fast paced spring semester! He's an amazing lecturer, easy professor, and an amazing human. Its easy to do well in the class and to enjoy learning the material without dying of stress.

analysis.name: Anthony Bloch
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Very good professor and course! The course uses ODE and geometric point of views to explain a lot of mechanical and physics phenomenon. The professor is very nice and always prepared. Office hours helps a lot for those who do not know much before. I learnt a lot even without taking much courses in analysis and geometry. Very inspiring overall.

Bloch had very useful office hours and would help explain the written homework, review questions, or recently learned concepts. Class was not always helpful, so go to office hours if you don't understand him. The book was often just as helpful as he was with general concepts. He sounds like Nigel Thornberry from "The WIld Thornberrys."

He's a nice guy but just a really bad lecturer. Exams and homeworks are not hard, but he fails to explain even the basic concepts in class and you don't know what he's even talking about most of the time, the only good thing about the class is the book, which he did a good job choosing for the class

Bloch is the man. During Calc 3, I hated it but now looking back it was actually a really great class, I always liked Bloch he's pretty good at teaching and is helpful, if you're going to take applied honors Cal 3 definitely take it with him

Professor Bloch is a great guy that challenges you in the hw assignments, but grades leniently and give fair exams. His lectures are very interesting and he has a very subtle humor. One of my favorite classes.

analysis.name: Joel Blum
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Easy, especially if you go to lecture and pay attention. Discussion activities are easy and can be done at home and turned in later (aka lab attendance is optional). Gives you all questions prior to exam. Interesting lecturer, great teacher!

Professor seems like a kind person, but lectures were pretty boring. The weekly quizzes weren't exactly tough but pays attention to minor details, some that are even irrelevant. Overall, class wasn't hard since there were no exmas.

Joel is a wonderful teacher. He spells out exactly what you need to know for the test on his lecture slides, and it is quite possible to get a great score on the test without reading the text because of the thoroughness of the lecture (still, the book was fun). Very accessible teacher and loves his work. Strongly recommended teacher and fun class.

Professor Blum has a lot of interesting career experience and passion to share. However, the restructuring of this course didn't work for me, personally. I would attend lectures but still do poorly on the weekly quizzes. With last-minute extra credit I got an A+, but feel I learned very little. Not the best intro to a really cool subject matter.

This class was fine. There was little direction, though. Lecture heavy with lots of group paper reading and presenting on it. Other than that, thee class is graded on an exam and a paper. Very knowledgable but the class was confusing.

analysis.name: Julio Blanco

review_highlights.comment: Blanco was completely unorganized. There was no clear grading scheme and he made the test extremely hard. He also has a very strong accent and cannot explain class material clearly. The worst!!

I was really excited to take this class as I thought it was an interesting topic. However, I had a very hard time understanding him because of his thick accent. Even his writing was unclear at times. The class was all exams that were heavily weighted towards multiple choice. He was willing to hear student concerns and accessible outside of class.

He pre-records videos for each chapter in replacement of lecture, but he still has lectures to discuss articles. Lecture times are mostly for office hours. The biggest challenge was definitely understanding him because of his thick accent. He frequently made errors in his answer key for exams. The class's grading scale is nice though. 85+  A

The worst class I have ever taken in the econ department (which is saying a lot). Extremely boring, material is pointlessly difficult, class drones on and on. A 1.5 hour lecture feels like 5 years. Will NEVER take a class with this guy ever again
He always asks if anyone has questions and goes through the material slowly. Easy grader

analysis.name: Deirdre Bloome
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Horrible, worst experience I've had.  Took this to get out of a math credit since I'm not a math major, and it was ridiculously hard for an "elementary statistics" course.  Unclear in her lectures, lazy, and gives hard tests that look at whether or not you can read trick questions and teach yourself.
Kind of snotty. Would not recommend. The tests are rather easy, especially with the curve. Gives off that ivy-league grad vibe like she treats you like you're dumb.

I'm majoring in Sociology because I never wanted to take math again, so I was terrified of this course. Professor seemed intimidating at first, but also REALLY smart, helpful. By the end I really came to like stats and learned a lot about how to work w/ data. Make no mistake, this is hard material and you will be challenged. But the payoff is huge.

Professor Bloome is amazing! I was apprehensive to take this course because I don't like math, but I am so happy that I did. She explains topics to make sure that everyone understands. There isn't too much homework and if you put in the work it will pay off. She does research as well on gender income inequality which is great. Office hours are good

She was an amazing professor who made coding accessible while still teaching statistics basics in great lectures. The homework was purposeful and her grading was clear and helped you improve. She genuinely cared about all her students and our success and was ready to help people solve issues with content and the class in general. I learned a lot.

analysis.name: Bogdan Popa
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Honestly one of the best professors I've had in the ME department. He really cares about you actually learning the material instead of memorizing or trying to use pattern recognition to solve problems. Exams are very resonable. He's also pretty good at explaining stuff.

Another perspective which is completely opposite of the review below me. The class was great. The exams are easy, he grades lightly, and he wants to help you learn the material. He is an overall nice professor who definitely cares about learning his students' names. I loved that Professor Popa went into depth in the derivation of formulas.

Prof. Popa is a very calm and collected person who explains material very clearly and at an appreciable pace. His exams can get tricky at times, but he grades based mostly on process, so arithmetic errors aren't a huge concern on exams. He also has two engaging MATLAB group projects which further our understanding of the course material.

Overall a nice guy who knows his stuff and teaches well. Made a point to learn the students' names. Very responsive to feedback. For example, some students asked that we work on more examples and he dedicated Fridays to working on exam style questions. Easy to reach at office hours. Exams, grading, and grading scale all very fair.

He is a very understandable professor. Content is tricky, but he teaches everything in a way where if you follow his steps, you will get a lot of partial credit on the exam even if you mess up. Care about students performing well, and will bump grades if you are close to cut-offs.

analysis.name: Benjamin Blankenship
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ben's a great GSI! You can tell he cares about his students because he's always offering additional help, direct feedback, or walking around checking up on tables during lab. Best GSI I've had at UMich so far! Grades fairly (and according to rubric) and you can always ask for feedback on the papers. Prepared for class and office hours are flexible!

Ben was great for Psych393Polsci 330! He was so helpful, and always had examples in section to help students understand the lecture material. Also, he always had interactive activities in class to help students immerse themselves in the material. "Online" participation (via twitter) is fun. DEFINITELY TAKE THIS CLASS -if you like psych of politics

Ben was easily the best GSI that I have had at UMich. He came to class prepared, and he was always willing to answer students' questions or meet during office hours. He truly wanted his students to succeed, and his calm personality helped the class run smoothly even when discussing some of the more difficult topics. I would highly recommend him!
Solid GSI, makes a really boring David Winter lecture enjoyable. One of the better psychology GSIs that I have had at Michigan. Good grader

Ben is the best GSI I have ever hard. He is not so much as an "easy grader" but more so understanding and VERY FAIR considering the level of the course. He is very easy to talk to and responds promptly. He really looks out for student's best interest. I can't thank him enough for a great semester!!!!!!!! A+++++++++++++++++++++++++++

analysis.name: James Bodiford
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bodiford was fantastic. He explained all the material clearly and thoroughly and was clearly very passionate about the subject. As long as you attend classes, you should get an A with very little difficulty. It's an interesting class if you're interested in music and science fiction, my favorite class I've taken at UMich!

At first I thought James was super dull in his teachings, but as the class material gets more interesting so does he. There were a ton of hilarious moments in the class and I'd definitely take James again if I was doing another music class.

Great class, great professor, the sci fi section is phenomenal! I will say though, highly reccomend you attend lectures so you won't fall behind in contents, which honestly I didn't have an issue with because the lectures are so easy to digest.

Fantastic professor and a fantastic course. The lectures were quite interesting and I learned a ton. Assignments are easy too and the projects were actually quite fun to work on as well. My only gripe is he sometimes cuts off people answering questions, and then later gets upset when no one raising their hand to answer questions. But yea he's cool.
Good professor and interesting lectures if you enjoy the content, but he grades a little stricter than I thought

analysis.name: Steven Bogaerts
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE FOR EECS 492! The class has been completely revamped and there is double the content crammed into the course with more depth and harder exams. The exams are nothing like whats shown in lecture. And this man just glosses over every mathematical formula during lecture like its nothing. Don't take this class or you will regret it.

DO NOT TAKE EECS492. This is the most content dense class I've ever taken. As an INTRO class, there is enough content to divide this course into two different ones. Exams are unfair and nothing like the practice ones. Lectures were packed with content and equations/graphs that were not talked about enough. Take 442, 388, or 445 instead.

While EECS 492 definitely got harder than past semesters, Professor Bogaerts was a great lecturer. He was very caring and thoroughly answered questions in class. I highly recommend going to class in person, as the content is a lot more digestible this way!

Despite provided online lecture, I went to in-person lecture just for Bogaerts. He was always kind and inspirational and you could tell he really wanted us to succeed. Although attendance was low in lecture, he always taught with the same amount of vigor and passion. His mantra "you belong here" actually helped me a lot over the semester.

Lectures were very informational and engaging. He obviously cares about the material and his students, and is very accessible outside of class hours. Great teacher for EECS 280, as long as you pay attention to lectures then you should be prepared for everything. He makes every student feel valued, and is willing to answer any question.

analysis.name: Bobby Madamanchi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Excellent lecturer for the data-oriented mastery course. Allows for a good deal of flexibility within the project specifications and provides ample support during and outside of class. Allows students to really concentrate on the project all semester and minimizes distractions. Provides time in class for group work, if needed. Good guest speakers.

Great professor and overall good guy, can be a bit experimental and freeform with lecture style and content, but the material is overall solid stuff - definitely helpful for high level coding patterns.

Beyond that, he has very clear grading criteria and is happy to help you do the best you can. 10/10 would take again.
The format of this class really didn't work for me - it was hard to follow along with what was happening. More structure would have been better.

Attend half of the lectures and get all late penalties waived, an absolutely wild deal but helps immensely with planning around other classes! This also means grading will take longer. Many assignments have clear rubrics and extra credit opportunities. He'll help prep for coding interviews, and the labs try too. Lab time could be made more valuable

analysis.name: David Brang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Definitely recommend for those who need a psych/neuro lab req. Lecture is not mandatory, exams are all open note, with free internet access and can be taken anywhere. Problem sets were intimidating at first because of the online software, but students are given step-by-step instructions on how to get full points.

Gave very dense, thorough lectures. It is clear he knows a lot about the field. Lecture content definitely went over my head at some points, but overall a good lecturer and clearly cares about his students.

He's a nice guy, clear slides and easy exams. The only issue is that he is extremely boring. His voice is super monotone and SOOOO slow, I would watch his lectures on 2x speed and be fine. I literally only went to the very first lecture and got an A in the class. It's an easy A but only take it if you're actually interested in EEG/want to study it

The course material is dense but he explains it in a way that makes it way easier. The exams weren't too hard and you can make a cheat sheet for them. He puts indicators on slides to tell which are the most important and which are background info, which makes studying for the exams very easy. Overall an excellent professor and course :)

Pretty nice guy. Only had 1 lecture a week, so not too much to gauge. The majority of the time he is just lecturing at you to get all the content in for you to use in the lab portion. The slides are crowded, but he usually provides the pdf with builds.
The lab isn't bad but that might depend on your GSI, and there's one partner presentation.

analysis.name: Patrick Boland
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Pat is concise. He instills confidence into your mathematic abilities. Pat always encourages students to find real-world applicability within the material covered in class, which seems rare among professors here. Overall, Pat is fair, patient, and smart; my level of understanding within calculus has increased dramatically since I've taken his class

He connected all topics to real-life examples, which made class fun. He didn't really explain topics that well in class - you are expected to do the readings/videos in order to learn in-depth. But, he was always accessible during office hours and genuinely made an effort to connect with you!

Pat does an amazing job of creating a light-hearted and constructive learning environment! This was my first calculus class at Michigan, and I am confident that this gave me a good foundation going forward. Highly recommend taking his section of Math 115 if you can!

Professor Boland is easily the best professor I've had at UMich. He's an engaging lecturer, helpful outside of class, and is overall a really great guy. He helped me through a very hard time in my college career and while my performance in this course wasn't what I had hoped, he was very reassuring and available to help me out.

Highly recommend taking Boland for 216. He is a great lecture and makes class interesting. Lecture and recitation do not have mandatory attendance, but both are basically necessary for doing well in the course. Boland knows what he is talking about and is very accessible with office hours as well.

analysis.name: Branko Kerkez
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Kerkez is hands down the best professor I have had at UMich so far. His lectures were always engaging, informative, and fun, and he put a ton of effort into his presentation of material. He also created an extremely laid-back atmosphere for the class. Even if you're not into Civil Engineering, take a class with him if you can. You'll have fun.

Professor Kerkez is a fantastic professor. He always keeps the class engaged and entertained and is reasonable at grading. You will have to work fairly hard for an A however. He is very kind outside of the classroom, and really puts an emphasis on the students. If I could give a 6/5 on RMP I would in a heartbeat.
An incredible engineering professor. He makes lectures extremely fun and engaging and deeply cares about student success.

CEE 373 (was CEE 270, switched Fall 17), taught by Branko Kerkez. Branko makes learning statistics actually enjoyable by using fun examples and genuinely cares about his students performance. His class has difficult material but he explains it in a way that makes it easy to understand. He will even slow down and repeat material if people are lost.

He is extremely knowledgeable, insightful and warm-hearted Professor. Extremely helpful, genuinely caring. Homeworks test the application of concept and are designed to connect with real world problems. Take home Midterm - a welcome break from traditional midterms; tests concepts comprehensively in the process of teaching new things.

analysis.name: Bruce Mannheim
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Being a linguistics major, I was excited for this class.  I had a great GSI and I enjoyed the readings.  The prof is completely useless, I didn't go to class and I got an A.  He's obsessed with the field work he did in Brazil in the '70's.  Lecture really has nothing to do with exams or paper.  Go to section and do the readings, you'll be fine.

Enjoys yelling at students for having newspapers or computers in class; draws attention to it and wastes class time. Talks quietly, he makes everything really complicated. He doesn't have anything to do with your grade so make sure you have a good GSI.

He does not grade anything you do all semester, leaving you guessing where you are in the class. You may think you are right on track, but the lack of feedback allows him to throw a curveball and give you a lower grade than you expected.
He's the worst professor I've ever had! He talks in a very confusing, complicated, and roundabout way, and rambles on about things that are boring, like his obession with Quechua.
readings and class are completely unrelated. lectures have nothing to do with topic of class. do NOT waste your time on this class if they don't change the professor.

analysis.name: Brian Kish
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I didn't have Kish as a professor, but I might have to start a campaign to build him a statue outside of GG Brown because his office hours single-handedly saved my grade in ME211. He is very caring, very respectful, and very willing to help anyone who may enter his office hours.

I love this guy. I almost wish I failed thermo just so I could be in his class again. He's absolutely incredible and cares so much about everyone. Lectures are very entertaining and he always gives out small gifts as a reward for doing in-class example problems. He does his job very well.
Amazing professor, cares a lot about his students and very clear lectures. exam grading also fair

KISH IS THE GOAT OF UOFM. lectures are great, and he's the only professor I've seen here that has kept attendance very high the entire year. The only bad thing about him is that he does not teach every course here.

Brian Kish had lectures complete with lots of relevant examples. He was very clear about what was important and included hands-on demonstrations so students could best visualize what we were learning in class. Be aware that exams are 75% of the course grade so try to maximize other components of your grade such as HW by going to office hours.

analysis.name: Heidi Buchele
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Heidi was tough, but when you're getting a license to help save lives, you have to be. She was excellent at providing feedback and facilitating class participation. I would take her class over and over again!

Heidi was a really fun professor to teach emergency response. This class has a lot of hands on activities and you have to go to class in order to get the certifications at the end of the semester. Each person (with a partner) gives a presentation for two topics in the course but as long as you meet with her she will tell you what to include.

Professor Heidi is very educated. She teaches everything very well and you will leave this class very educated. I loved this class for learning more about how to care for emergencies. She does make sure to practice a lot with us; but she does expect us to know the answers and she is pretty caring for situations. She will let you make up if needed
This class was fun, and Heidi is a good teacher. However, she can be loud and sometimes it may feel as though her comments on your work is personal (it's not, that is just her teaching style).

While it is easy to get an A and more of a fun class, Heidi is stressful to have as a teacher. She consistently calls on random people to answer questions but also gets mad at pretty much anything anyone does. I guess it can be good for learning but I found her to be pretty rude and impatient most of the time. Her class definitely is an experience.

analysis.name: Dominique Butler-Borruat
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining

analysis.name: Jowei Chen
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Brilliant and witty. Very engaging discussions in class and sharp, but he will also take the piss out of you if you make an argument that is not completely well thought out. One of the most interesting professors I have ever had.

Such a fun person to take a class from. Professor Chen has a disarming way of making fun of himself in class, which is hilarious because he's teaching about redistricting court cases where he actually played a huge role. Such an interesting guy and an amazing experience to learn about election law from someone who's working on it in the real world.

Truly one of the best Professors I have ever had. The course is very engaging, and Dr. Chen really lives what he teaches, especially with redistricting. The course is not super hard - just 5 essays. I never skipped class, and participated a lot because I found the course material interesting. Sad that Dr. Chen is not teaching Winter 2026!

I can say without a shadow of a doubt that Professor Chen is one of the best professors at the University (and my personal favorite). He gives all of his lectures off the dome, is hilarious, and approaches all material from as unbiased a standpoint as possible (even though he makes his views known from the get-go). Amazing professor!

My favorite prof I've ever had at Michigan. He is so funny and even though his class is all lecturing, he keeps you engaged the whole time. The readings are just cases, so if you're interested in law, you should like them. He lectures off the top of his head and it's clear he's an expert.

analysis.name: Amy Cell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: A great lecturer! Definitely new to teaching but super knowledgable and ready to help her students.

She gives everyone A, only her 'favorites' will get A+. She intentionally changed my marks from 10/10 to 0/10 after 1 month just so I could get an A as I wasn't her favorite student. I emailed her and she said she did it by mistake and that she will revert it but never did that. Everyone else gets A too, had I known that I wouldn't have put efforts

Her lectures are amazing. She has so much experience being out in the corporate world, managing people and projects. Almost every lecture had an anecdote from her past work with a strong message. The group project and class blend really well. You actually apply what you learn from her lecture while working with your client.

Overall a great class if you are an engineering grad student who needs a course to reach full time status, balance your course load, and boost your GPA. Attendance is graded, so don't plan on skipping class regularly. However, the lectures are interesting and worth attending. Easy A if you do the work.

analysis.name: Celia Schultz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was a massive disappointment (and I love the topic). So many tedious writing assignments and extremely pointless 20-minute timed essays. Discussion is useless. Very picky grading. Lectures are impossible to follow with essentially no slides and a copious amount of rambling. If you want to learn about Rome, take CLCIV 202 or HISTORY 201.

I had her for CLCIV 302- Worst class of my academic career. She was the most boring lecturer of all time. Furthermore, she made us buy her expensive book to read from. The check-ins were worth 40% of the class and they were graded like they were the most important thing since Jesus. absolutely terrible. Readings were never ending. Never take her.

She's a nice person, but the class was pretty rough. We had four 20-minute in-class essays. Her slides are AWFUL so if you don't show up, you won't understand anything. The slides have barely any words and she talks a ton. The final is key terms (there are hundreds given to us- impossible), a timeline, two essays, and a huge map all in two hours.

Highlights: -5% of class grade reduced if you miss "spot-check" attendance -Grading based on ability to regurgitate exactly what she says in lecture (word for word) -Expects you to memorize an insane amount of information -Doesn't post slides I'm a student taking 18 academic credits and this 4 credit course was over half of the reading I had to do

Professor Schultz does a great job balancing the totality of Roman Monarchical and Republican History with fun and engaging lectures.  The course is extremely content-dense, but she manages to break it up into nice chunks that are supported by primary source readings. She also does a good job of making the course AI proof, so lectures are 100% req.

analysis.name: Carlos Cesnik
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Cesnik was a great professor.  He really cared about the students, and that showed through.  Unfortunately I took it at 8:30 AM, so the students weren't terribly energetic which frustrated him, but he's super helpful and really wants you to learn.  Sure, it's challenging material, but work with him, and you can master it.

If you're like myself and most people and can't stand structures, take this guy. He's probably the best possible structures prof. you can get, though it's not a very easy class by any means. Don't get the book, you won't need it. At least I didn't. He has pretty good notes, so unfortunately you can't miss his class.

Prof. Cesnik is one of the better profs I've had so far at Michigan.  He is a very likable guy and he knows the subject very well.  The class is not that difficult if you go to lecture and take good notes...the book is worthless so don't waste your money.

He's quite famous for structure guy but NEVER for 481. I'm doubtful if he fully understands what he is teaching, as he often leaves the lecture to GSIs from Prof. Martins' lab. Seriously with Prof. Martins were teaching this semester as usual.
Good guy but pretty heinous class. He asks questions on exams that are way harder than we can be expected to complete in the given time. I was lucky to escape with an A-

analysis.name: Celeste Brusati
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's a really nice lady but she is a bit of a boring lecturer. There is not much reading in the class, but the finals require a ton of memorization. Interesting subject matter though.

Celeste rarely actually lectures in her own class, which seems pretty backwards. Frequent quest speakers and sometimes the quest speakers give no relevant information in their lectures. Nice person, but not an overwhelmingly good teacher. She's also obsessed with Dutch painters, so get ready to hear a lot about those.

She seemed like an ok professor but she never really lectured. There was almost always a guest lecturer so we never knew what we were going to get during class. Some were interesting, some were boring. The exams aren't hard, as long as you study describing paintings with friends. The exam questions were all brand new, so there was nothing to review

She has certain things expected from each student. When I went to her office hour to consult with my research paper, she gave many (not that helpful) resources. You have to figure out what she wants to see in your paper. This class was a small-size seminar type class held once a week so if you skip one, she will definitely notice.
One of those Shaman Drum-only hippies.  Not terribly organized, but overall not bad.

analysis.name: Abigail Celis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: In her first semester at Penn State, she surprised me with her course. I'm a senior in a 100 level French history elective, and her class was doable. If you come to class prepared, and engage in the class, its an easy A. No textbook required. Shes a soft spoken prof, and willing to help her students, you just have to be willing to put in work.

Celis is a professor who is a little more soft spoken, but is knowledgeable about her subject.  Shes got a good sense of humor if you participate and engage in class.  Her grading is fair, but the work load is heavy, and she cares that you come prepared with the homework.  Overall, she made a subject I'm not crazy about pretty bearable.

Overall her class just bored me to tears. I was really interested to take a class about hipsters because its such an unconventional topic, but everything she talked about was so generic it made me not even want to do the work (which was way too heavy for a freshman seminar anyway).
She's soft-spoken and she is a really nice person.

analysis.name: Erin Cech
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cech has opened my mind to so much in the course of Sociology/Women's Studies 447. She is very extremely intelligent, respectful, and professional. Her lectures are always organized and intriguing. I've been recommending this course to everyone. Honestly, this has been my favorite course so far, and I'm not a Soc or Women's Studies major.

Professor Cech is AMAZING. Soc 447 has been the best class I have taken so far. She provided really interesting material in lecture that was different than I have gotten in most soc/women's studies classes. She is really nice and energetic. Reading material and attending class is a must because she doesn't post slides online. But totally worth it!

Easily the best class I've taken here.  She's super nice and professional and intelligent and all of the course material was engaging.  She's also receptive to student feedback and actually seems to enjoy teaching unlike some of the profs at this university.
Sociology of Gender was my favorite class of the semester due to the interesting lectures and readings as well as Professor Cech's sunny disposition. Take a class with her if you can.

analysis.name: Rosario Ceballo
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS, ESPECIALLY IF YOU ACTUALLY LIKE CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY. She might as well be teaching counseling psych, calls people seeking mental health treatment "seriously disturbed" and puts questions on her exams about the color of M&M's in her story in class. Pointless, offensive, shouldn't be teaching clinical psychology.

I took this last semester and it was AWFUL.  She had no compassion for mentally ill patients and made that very clear.  Also, she is incredibly detail oriented in all the worst ways.  She basicallye xpects you to memorize details so long as they have no thing to do with anything else.  HORRIBLY BORING, also.

This class was very detail specific.  Only really 3 grades count (2 exams and a movie paper) not much to help if you do bad on the first exam.  It's a small lecture class, although there is no attendence if you miss class, you miss a lot.  The book is important and takes a lot straight from the book.

One of the hardest Psych class I've taken simply because Dr. Ceballo writes very detailed exams.  Although we don't have a textbook, she assigns a LOT of supplemental readings and expects you to memorize the details.  The exams questions are very specific regarding the assigned readings.

Really interesting course. She is really nice and makes lectures interesting. Essays are fun to write but she does grade harshly. Exams are very detail specific and tough. Definitely do the readings and go to class and take notes!!! But overall I do recommend the class(:

analysis.name: Eleanor Clowney
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I was honestly afraid to take this professor, but I'm glad I signed up for her course. Even though she is lecture heavy, her first exam was fair. Her office hours are great, and she really assists you with the content you're confused about. She appreciates it when students seek help, and she is very passionate about the content she teaches.

She'll start off by giving a simple definition of a topic, and then we will go from 0 to 100 out of no where like it's common knowledge. Impossible to follow in lecture, uses unnecessary terms, goes over 20+ topics in a single lecture, overall terrible teaching style. Only reason to show up is for the mandatory iClicker points. Do not take.

I had Professor Clowney for my first half of Biology 172. She convinced me there was something wrong with me. I did everything recommended to succeed, but she taught everything out of order and assumed everyone in the introductory biology class had a Ph.D. in Biology. Her exam questions were purposely meant to confuse you. Avoid at all costs.

She literally reads off of the slides and doesn't elaborate, if she does, it is impossible to understand. Office hours is no help either, if she's discussed something in OH before, she won't go over it again. Worst prof I've EVER had tbh you're in for one if you take her class, although the second prof is much better. Self teach only option to pass

This professor does not care about you. Even the head of the bio department announced that the exams that she has written and lectured on have had the "worst grades he has ever seen in his decades of teaching". She instructed so poorly that they had to curve the class and for the first time in program history added points to the exam.

analysis.name: Sally Clegg
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor, definitely my favorite from this semester. She is incredibly kind and helpful and will give you very useful feedback. Participation does matter in her grading process but as long as you participate in class, show effort, and generally just show up you are almost guaranteed a good grade.
My goat. Super sweet, can be a tough grader for some projects but nothing crazy. Super understanding and gives great critiques.

Sally was a fantastic professor. She is very methodical and organized in her teaching. There were only a couple of projects in the class, which made grading difficult, but she gave enough time for students to go back and make revisions if they were unhappy with a grade. Be prepared to work frequently outside of class.
She was very well organized and helpful. We learned a solid amount of foundation but was still given plenty of creative freedom.
Sally is incredibly insightful, clear in her instructions, and kind. She has high expectations but also provides a lot of guidance and feedback, so expect to be pushed in her class!

analysis.name: Laura Clapper
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: if i could pick one person to represent the human race to an alien population, i'd pick laura clapper. and the aliens would love us.

Laura is a wonderful professor who truly cares about her students. W300 is self-graded, so as long as you work hard, you'll get an A. Laura has high expectations, but meeting them has significantly improved my writing.

Love, love, LOVE Laura. Take any classes you can with her. One of the most genuine people I have ever met in my life. She is kind without being coddling, and both expects and truly wants the best from her students.

Laura is a wonderful professor, who really cares about her students. She will provide excellent feedback to help you improve your reading, writing, and analytical skills. It's important to participate and stay on top of assignments. If I could take her again, I would.
Just don't take her classes; unsympathetic and not understanding. So many pointless assignments that are time consuming and obnoxious.

analysis.name: Steven Clark
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 131 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He taught the course for the second half, and I really think 90% of the people in the class have no recollection of what he taught. He runs through huge concepts and honestly makes no sense. The average on his exam was a 68! A 68! Unheard of in an intro class. Just to top it all off, he didn't get an ovation on the last day of class. Avoid. AVOID.

If you're an AP/Transfer starting at UM-AA on the fence about taking this class: know Prof. Clark is patient, passionate, very accessible, and truly an expert; his smaller class size makes iClicker, Study Groups, and Discussions easy points just for showing up—also allows for a personal connection. I honestly dont know anyone who regrets taking it!

Clark's good during lecture! He's much less monotone than people claim. It's outside of lecture where I have a problem. He's very rude to students asking concept questions on piazza. He'll answer with things like "that's a good question" and "rewatch the last three lectures." He's very unapproachable during office hours. And, his exams are harder.

Genuinely one of my favorite professors. He explained content really well and was passionate. His exams were usually accurate to the lectures. I also liked the way discussion was structured to not be overwhelming. He also gave a good amount of extra credit. Overall, as long as you understand the content (not just memorize), you'll be all good.

I would avoid this class and professor at all costs. He told us after our third exam that the class would be heavily curved but would never tell us what the curve would be and wouldn't even give an idea of it. He then basically took back the curve after we took our final and only adjusted the grading scale by 1%. Disrespectful and condescending.

analysis.name: Claudia Creed
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is really passionate about what she teaches but struggled to connect with students and get them to participate in the class I had. Even so, she always tried her best. Know that she is a slow grader. Would not necessarily recommend.

Decent lecturer. Lots of reading, but it's not THAT deep. Lenient on midnight deadlines which was helpful. Fair grader. Lots of writing (bc it's a writing class), but she's super reasonable and understanding. I was a little scared after reading the single rating on this website, but she's super fair, which is all someone could ask for.

Claudia was a decent lecturer but struggled to engage the class at times. Her one-on-one conferences often lacked clarity, with repeated points filling time rather than offering useful feedback. Her biggest issue was grading delays—waiting six weeks for feedback made it difficult for students who wanted to do redrafts.

Professor Creed is so incredibly nice. She really cares about her students. There's a bit of group work with peer edits. Overall the class was pretty easy with only three essays and very little other work.

- Never graded anything on time. 
- Lectures were boring 
- Accessible outside of class and lenient on deadlines

analysis.name: Marin Kristen Clark
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
(EARTH 351) I learned a TON but the class is a train wreck

-Blames the class for being behind but doesn't make assignments on time
-Labs are HARD AF
-Rude to students in class
-Class order is poor
-Homework is convoluted
-Lectures are FAST, must attend to do well
-Thorough compression REQUIRED for exam

Clearly well respeced, but horrible teacher.

This is a 2 credit class...and it was one of my worst grades. Not clear about what will be on the exam and exams are extremely hard! I received Cs on two of the three exams and an A on the one when she was absent and we were taught by another prof.  Def dont take this class unless you wanna feel dumb for not doing will in a 2 credit course

Professor Clark seems very nervous at times, and she has difficulty explaining the material.  The quizzes and exams cover material that is not well explained in lecture and cannot be found in the textbook.  Therefore, it is tough to answer some of the questions on the various assignments.  Overall, I do not recommend taking this class.

Marin typifies the very driven/intelligent but also entitled ivy-league-educated academic. When things are not done exactly her way she is RUDE, sometimes boarding on abusive. She tends to be controlling and micromanaging. She lives in an internally generated bubble of constant stress that very few are immune to getting caught up in.

She's really nice and is very passionate about her work. It's annoying that this class is only two credits because you have to study a fair amount to get an A on the exam. If you put in the studying hours, you will get an A.

analysis.name: Clifford Lampe
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ironically, for a class built on gamification, this class is designed really poorly.  Ten 2-4 page writing assignments (which you get little to no helpful feedback for your grade).  2 large projects, 1 semester-long project, weekly pop quizzes (on specific details from the 4 hours worth of reading), final exam.  Don't take this.  HIGHLY SUBJECTIVE

Cliff uses Gradecraft for his class - a program that attempts to turn an academic course at a major university into a video game. The course is structured in a way that is made to let students work at their own pace and instead the teacher drops all of the assignments on you at once. He has planned this class very poorly and I was jk about him hot

Professor Lampe stepped up after our previous professor couldn't teach anymore for personal reasons, and he's been nothing but fair and accommodating. Yes, there were quite a few readings but you really just had to skim them. The tests were also curved so as long as you put in a little effort you'd do well. The final project was also manageable.

Absurd amount of work. 100 + pages of reading per week. obscure pop quiz every week. 10 2-4 page essays, 2 projects equivalent to 10 page essay, another 2500 word essay. no assignments relate to actual material you need to know. will ruin your life. required to go to out of class lectures to complete essays. will be biggest regret of your life.

The GSI's are horrible graders, their feedback is not clear. I don't understand how they grade these assignments. Be prepared for a lot of reading and it will not be helpful for the quizzes. The lectures are very boring. It seems like a lot of the topics are random and do not connect to each other. I wouldn't take this class if not needed.

analysis.name: Marcus Collins
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Every lecture feels like a TED Talk - very engaging, but when you ask him to clarify something, he just repeats his TED talk and expects you to understand. This goes for if you ask questions in class or if you go to office hours. 

He is also very accomplished and will make sure you know it, which comes off as full of himself.

While his lectures are inspirational and great.  He grades pretty tough and doesn't grieve feedback on what he grades.  Additionally assignments he graded in our class were graded and returned a week later less that 3 hours in some cases before the next assignment was due.  There was also zero feedback so mistakes were repeated commonly.
hes good and inspirational but lowkey is not a proactive teacher/accessible at all

Multiple huge assignments from very beginning to very end that take forever. You must purchase his book as the main reading for the course. Every class uses the same examples and language from his book. He also doesn't share slides and for projects later in the semester, you are required to incorporate and utilize course concepts

Marcus has a stellar reputation amongst Ross students, and somehow manages to even exceed that reputation. His classes are wildly difficult to get into for a reason. You can tell how much he cares for students to an incredible extent, even going as far as to give his personnel phone number to students. By far the greatest course I have ever taken.

analysis.name: Corey Powell
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Corey seems like a cool guy. However, any enjoyment I may have had doing stats had been sucked out of this class. There's an ungodly amount of homework and work you need to do outside of class just to understand the content. I've seen more words than numbers in this class. You also have to learn R coding, which is stupid. I don't recommend!

Please listen to the other people. I was one who thought the other people were being dramatic. It is very important you listen to them and me. Corey Powell makes this class way too complicated for no reason and barely tries to explain it so people understand. I took AP Stats and got a 4, but I feel like I have never taken a statistics class.

Quite frankly, he doesn't understand how to teach stats. Lectures are not specific, unclear, present material in illogical orders, don't teach statistics in line with other courses, over-emphasize by-hand calculations. Uses few examples and almost exclusively speaks in conceptual terms. Got a 5 on AP STAT exam and was often confused in this class.

Took this class in FA24. Is he good at explaining everything? No, not ALL the contents. However, with some knowledge in AP Stats and all the extra credits he gives for all assignments (it was very doable to have some errors but still get over 100%), it's not very hard to get an A. The exams are also easier than the covered contents.

Do not take any class with Corey Powell. Just take 250 even if you took AP stats I promise you it is not worth it. The examples in lectures are SO different from what is on the exam and he is really not great at answering questions clearly. Again, just take 250. I took AP in HS and that wasn't helpful bc of how confusing Corey Powell made things.

analysis.name: Maria Cotera
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She only lectures half of the semester and the rest is done by GSIs. The readings are a bit boring but you only need to skim them to get good grades on quiz. It is very important to invest effort to section participation and group project (don't make your project boring if you want good grades). Midterm was takehome exam and there was no final exam

Easy to get an A in this class, just skim through the readings for the online quizzes and go to class (but you don't have to take notes because you don't have any tests on lecture material). But I didn't really care for Prof Cotera. She had a pretty heavy bias during lectures and came off as arrogant.

Her graduate level courses are rather boring and are not really engaging. I don't think her teaching style is for me as her class is all over the place. Students who are new to grad school or theory based courses prepare to feel like an imbecile and confused! This comment is based on one of her UT Austin courses

EASY A! But--worst class I've taken at U of M. Opinion based quiz questions, little respect for other epistemological approaches. I'm a liberal, and this was way too far for me. Cherry picking data, little critical thinking, 100 pgs reading/week. Lecture required, no laptops. Belittle opinions. If interested in WOMENSTD, take different course.

She made the lectures interesting and I really liked the class even though I don't agree with everything she taught. My GSI was also very accepting of conflicting viewpoints. There are a lot of readings but you just have to skim them for answers to the online quizzes. The midterm is take home and you work on the final project the whole semester.

analysis.name: Aline Cotel
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: "A River Runs Through It" was an interesting class, and she was very knowledgeable in a lot of areas. Sometimes the examples she would do in class were confusing, but they were never too hard to understand since they were always posted on canvas.

you can tell she's very knowledgeable in this field. the maths was never too hard and she was available after class. sometimes her explanations were so so but nothing too bad. and she is decently nice and funny.

"A River Runs Through It" is an incredible class with an incredible instructional team, especially Prof. Cotel. Her enthusiasm, passion, experience, care, and understanding made this class a blast, even when it was difficult to grasp concepts or remain balanced with other coursework, activities, and average college student problems.
Very nice professor and is willing to provide help if you ask. Lectures can get boring, and they're not always applicable to homework/tests, but they aren't mandatory.

I took Aline's River Runs Through It ENGR 100 course. I wasn't too interested in environmental engineering but it was kind of interesting and probably one of the easiest sections of ENGR 100. It's very easy to get by. I knew that some of the labs would be outside, but I forgot that this is Michigan and it was very cold at the beginning. Dress right

analysis.name: Colleen Crane

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Crane seems to have a solid amount of experience and knows what she's talking about but as a grader and teacher she's almost impressively unhelpful, she graded harshly based off of having a self-admitted bad night and provided no practical feedback as a result. Don't take her if you want to learn, take her if you want to listen to her talk.

Yes, Colleen Crane is knowledgeable about assessment, and I learned a lot. However, I would have rather stayed home. I hated attending this class, and it should have been my favorite. Collen was rude and condescending, grilling students about clients and judging us for not knowing enough. She would be the least encouraging therapist ever

There aren't too many assignments in this course and some are worth a lot of points. She makes clear her expectations for these assignments so if you try, you will be graded fairly and graciously. Colleen is extremely knowledgable and I think that was what I enjoyed most about her as a professor. I would absolutely take her course again.

Professor Crane is outstanding. Well prepared. Ready to engage students. Never boring. But most of all she is fair and does not push her personal and political beliefs on students, as most professors in the School of Social Work do. I wish I could take every class with her. She works hard to help students learn. Excellent!

Most boring class ever. Lectures never ending, all she does is talk the whole time. No break out groups to discuss in smaller groups, no activities, nothing. Just lecture. Would not recommend taking her if you get bored easily. Too much information in each lecture, none retained at end of lecture.

He's super nice, but when I took the class, it seemed that he wasn't quite sure how to command a room, which made him sometimes hard to follow. One-on-one time with him was extremely helpful, though, and he explained how he did the best with what he was given for class.

Dr. DC is really nice and I did enjoy this class. But everytime I asked him or the GSI a question, they didn't know the answer and would just tell me to leave my programming how it was. This was really frustrating. Lectures were boring too.
Very nice, not a great helper despite his best efforts

review_highlights.comment: She only taught the latter half of the course so it was a slight adjustment. I did like that her lectures were more organized & cohesive, and she didn't linger on any topic longer than needed. Take good notes during lecture! Answered questions in class well and clearly stated what to know for exams. Gave extra credit bc class averages were too low.

Dr. C is a kind and caring professor. I never had a problem understanding her or felt she went too fast in lecture, like others have said. Lectures are recorded anyways. She explained concepts well and pointed out important info. Pay attention to the lectures, do the practice exams + problem roulette. We were allowed to have cheat sheets for exams.

She seems like a very nice person, however, I ended up doing much better Chapman's half of the course. The test avg for Chapman was anywhere from 72-75, whereas Exam 3 (w her) the class average was 68%. You can tell she loves teaching what she does, however, she goes WAY too fast and taking notes was a pain.

Dr. Csankovszki was very interested in the material she taught. Reading the textbook was entirely optional. My major complaint is that she moved very fast. If you get lost in a lecture the rest of that lecture made no sense. When you were able to keep up, she was very clear and makes a lot of sense. Lecture recordings are your friend with her.
Professor Gyorgyi was a bit more clear than professor Chapman, but the exams were still really really tough. REMEMBER TO STUDY YOUR BUTT OFF!

analysis.name: Felipe Csaszar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Excellent class.  Made difficult and dry concepts simple. would love to take another class with him.

Professor Csaszar was excellent. He's a tough grader, but his lectures are efficient, on point, and thorough. He was able to cut through clutter and direct the course to the essence of the material. I highly recommend taking a course with him.

Professor Csaszar is nice, but his lectures were boring. I had another strategy prof at Ross and he was much more interactive and engaging, and he seemed better at encouraging students to expand on their ideas while helping them understand their limitations. Maybe it's unfair that I'm comparing the 2, but prof Csaszar didn't meet my expectations.
Well, I love Felipe's instruction during offie hours.  He make me interested in world economy.  A must-take
Best professor at UofM. Really clear lectures, interesting readings.

analysis.name: Ctirad Uher
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 73 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor. Take him if you have the chance! He definitely makes a difficult course more manageable. Exams are difficult but if you do extra book problems in addition to the assigned ones, you should be fine.

Perhaps Usher was better in the past, but essentially teaching is to load a lot of information in slides and walk you through practice problems. I had trouble staying awake, and tho I did well I don't feel like I have a good understanding of thermo or relativity. To succeed, just cram all practice problems a week before 45% weighted final exam

Class was super interesting but there are problemslike the fact that the final is worth 45% of the grade. The homework aremultiple choice easy questions. His lectures can get boring since he reads off walls of text and it is really hard to stay awake in his lectures. Overall he is pretty good. Only take this class if you are good at test taking.

Took this class for fun and it paid off. Very funny and smart professor. Lectures flew by with him teaching them, but they were very content-heavy. It's smart to attend class, that's what really helped me out along the way! Make sure to do the practice problems at the end of the slides if you still don't get the material. Overall, highly recommend!

Lecture style is reading huge paragraphs on slides talking through book explanations/example problems, so some explanations on hard concepts left some understanding to be desired. Doesn't answer questions well, so you're better off looking it up later. Two tests are 70% of your grade which is very unforgiving for small mistakes. Easy class overall.

analysis.name: Craig Rodriguez-Seijas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I love the content of the course, but felt as though Dr.R's way of teaching was very reductive to it. He is a very strict behaviorist and belittles other schools of thought. He makes weird remarks during class about certain psychiatric populations. I would still take it, but just wanted to say because it definitely caught me off guard.

Phenomenal professor! Read before lecture, and go to office hours; he's super helpful. Also, the review on Apr 2nd, 2025, is just straight up lying. He does NOT expect you to memorize every disorder, and even specified that in class. Focus on the disorders we spent the most time on, and just generally understand the others, and you'll be all good!

Craig is very knowledgeable about the topic so I learned a lot from this class. There are three exams and two papers about two books you have to read. We have had around seven pop quizzes for 5 points each, but he takes the average score and drops your lowest one. Readings from the textbook are long but very important to do well on the exams.

Abnormal psych has been my favorite psych class I've taken. He does talk really fast, but there is a lot to get through in lecture. Everything that is on the exam is based off what we learn in class, and the textbook we read just helps reiterate what we already talked about. He wants you to succeed so always talk to him if you need too!

Dr. Rodri-Seijas is truly one of my favorite professor here at UofM, his lectures are pretty direct and exams are all covered by what lecture suggest. My only issue is that whenever you raise your hand to ask a question, he will quickly cut you off before you finish the question which I see as disrespectful but it is not a big problem.

analysis.name: Hayley Crowell
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super nice prof, great lecturer. Don't use the textbook, it's repeat info of what's covered in lecture. Lecture consists of practice problems since you watch lecture videos over the weekend. The problems are the same level as exams but she's very slow giving/explaining them. Attendance is iclicker (participation, not accuracy) so u can do from home

Dr. Crowell is very kind and is clearly very passionate about what she teaches. Her "real" lectures are all online, and the in-person classes are really just review questions using iClicker (she calls these ALS). I wasn't a huge fan of this format but I don't think it's in her control. She answers to emails very quickly and politely. Love her!

Dr. Crowell is the goat of BIO171, her lectures are very clear and she also takes time to go over things requested by students. I was also lucky enough to have her for discussion as well and you can really tell how passionate she is about what she teaches and how much she wants everyone to succeed. Absolutely sweetest person ever, TAKE HER CLASS!

I took Bio 171 with her, and she was amazing! You can tell she really loves the content she is teaching and really cares that her students understand everything. Despite having so many students, she really does take the time to get to know you and give personal advice if given the opportunity. Highly recommend taking Bio with her!

Dr. Crowell was a great teacher and cared deeply about her students. She is very passionate and knowledgeable about biology! The class isn't necessarily an easy one and you definitely have to put in the extra work for a good grade but Dr. Crowell makes it much more comprehendible! I would definitely recommend her!

analysis.name: Christopher Crowder
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: I took LSWA 125 for my writing requirement freshman year and this was easily my favorite (and easiest) class and professor. Chris gives amazing feedback on essays and projects and wants his students to succeed. He is usually a very light grader and gives very open project and essay guidelines giving you a lot of freedom.

Professor Crowder was one of my favorite professors I took my Freshman year at UMich. The readings before class were optional, but they were honestly interesting and added so much to the lesson the next day if you had the spare time to look at them. Overall, amazing guy and fun teacher. 100% recommend, and would love to take again.

Chris is incredibly caring and super supportive of his students. His class allows you to create projects you are passionate about and receive thoughtful feedback and encouragement. Readings for class can get long but are always interesting. I could not more highly recommend taking a course with Chris, easily my favorite professor I've had so far.

Chris was easily my favorite professor I have had so far. He is so kind and I was always excited to go to class. I took Writing 160 food for thought and he made the class so fun that I considered getting a minor in writing so I could keep taking his classes. 10000% recommend, the class was so easy and a really interesting place to be.

really sweet guy!! class is super easy, the easiest out of all the lswa classes in my experience. the readings are a lot but they are genuinely interesting and it's pretty easy to bluff your way through it. i didn't have time to read the last half of the semester and was totally fine. very chill grader.

analysis.name: Ralph Crisci
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
