review_highlights.comment: Great professor! Super kind and caring to his students and was super helpful during office hours. All of the GSIs were also very helpful. Grading is very exam-heavy but if you go to lecture, do the homework, and go to office hours to ask any questions, it is very manageable!
Great professor and honestly awesome guy. Teaches tough content in a digestible way. Really cares about his students and wants them to succeed
Ralph is amazing. He's extremely approachable and is very respectful of students. He makes the class fun and wants to see students succeed.

Dr. Crisci was a great professor that explained material clearly. He taught with a moderate pace, and exams were very representative of what we learned in class. Homework, discussion, and exam reviews are excellent resources to help you prepare for exams and are even worth a portion of your grade. Just don't fall behind, and you will do well!

Lectures were pretty good and covered everything you need, the only thing is he went kinda slow and took a lot of questions from the class, so our section was always behind for the exams. He is a nice guy and also cracked some funny jokes, and I turned out just fine for the exams by reading class notes and the textbook.

analysis.name: Sara Crider
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is mostly led by students, we only really see Sara during our first meeting, and when she monitored one of our seminars to see how we're doing. But overall, I highly recommend this class, it was a real blast having those close discussions with other classmates. The homework shouldn't be as bad, if you're fine with reading long passages.

ALA 122 is a great class! There was a lot of reading listed, but I didn't do much of it and still got an A. Sara is an awesome professor who really cares about her students. Highly recommend ALA 122 for getting those social science distribution credits. super easy class, very worthwhile

ALA122 is a student-led dialogue class, but their training came from Sara. It would be practically impossible not to get an A in this class (really, everyone would finish with a 100 if the IGR program wasn't against giving out an A+). Sara assigned the readings for this class, and planned the activities, and nothing was too challenging.

Sara has been probably one of the most inspirational lecturers at UMich. Despite my major not falling under the social sciences, I really enjoyed her class of ALA 220, and I would strongly recommend taking it with her. The skills and knowledge from this course I will carry into my future career.

Overall I like Sara. She is very passionate about what she teaches and she is honestly very nice. If you read her other reviews from Eastern, she is scattered & do not expect to get your grades back. Those that you do receive, she is a tough grader. Participation does matter. Just do the readings and put some effort in & you'll be fine

analysis.name: Cristhian Espinoza-Pino
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

Cristhian is interesting and I learned a lot about economics from him, but he gets frustrated easily during office hours if you don't understand him right away. He got me interested in something that I had already wanted to explore. Challenging, but informative. Take Indigenous Activism in the Age of Globalization if you can!

Cristhian is an extremely interesting professor. He facilitated fascinating discussions that challenged me to think analytically in a way I haven't previously. His participation expectations will initially seem high, but as long as you are actively engaged and contributing to discussion you will be fine. I highly recommend taking a class with him!

Cristhian was definitely one of the nicest professors I've ever had. I was really intimidated by him at first- he does come off as kind of authoritarian - but he's kind and supportive and very helpful if you go to office hours. He's very intelligent & doesn't get paid enough for all the work he does. He's opinionated, but it makes class interesting

analysis.name: Brian Coppola

Coppola is good enough to make the lectures understandable, but is always concerned with reinforcing his superiority over students. Not the most approachable in my opinion. Would've rather taken this class with Nolta even if it meant waiting another semester.

analysis.name: Javier Cravino

If I could give him 0, I would.

Dr. Duan does not teach. You go to the lecture to get confused by whatever he says. He gaslights you and commonly says "Biology is very easy" and "just read the textbook". analysis.name: Annica Cuppetelli

wanted to see if garment design/construction was something i was interested in, and annica was the perfect person to help guide me! the attendance criteria is insane though, and i was criticized for missing class even with a doctors note.

I took this class online but this was one of the best online classes I took this semester- Annica did her best to provide as much in depth instruction as possible even over an online format and I really appreciated it. She can grade a bit tough but it is honest and she gives great feedback and will direct you to helpful sources. Highly recommend!

analysis.name: Julie Cushman
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I liked Julie! She is easy to reach and talk to. The class had many good discussions. It was generally quite easy and we covered a lot, but all quite broadly. I am disappointed in the quality of her teaching, and I feel as though I learned more from the other students in the class rather than the professor herself.

The class was chaotic and disorganized. It was difficult to identify what we were talking about and why. Guest speakers were scheduled and their schedules changed frequently leading to repeated changes sometimes on the day of which then affected the synchronous and asynchronous times. Leaving me further confused.

This lecturer is rigid to the point that she makes our entire class anxious about our learning. She is very knowledgeable about research. She intentionally over-complicates the lecture content. She does not seem to want you to succeed in her course. I will discourage taking her courses to anyone. Your learning is guaranteed to be frustrating.

She talks a lot, requires tons of readings, and does not grade anything until the very end of the semester. She promised feedback for a month straight only giving it to us days before a group project was due. She gets sidetracked very easily and much of the lecture is not important to the assignments. Little to no discussion in a 3 hour long class.

lectures are recorded, but not uploaded in timely manner. hw are good balance of doable and challenging. tests are predictable: review hw and make sure to pay attention in class because sometimes he drops hints about possible exam questions. put everything you can on your cheat sheet; who knows if you'll need it.

Prof. Cutler is a nice guy, but the class is very disorganized. On many occasions he forgets to post homeworks, and he would also randomly cancel class. His lectures are not helpful at all, and he goes on long tangents. Use the book to learn. The exams can range from not that bad to literally impossible to finish. Overall the class is just chaotic.
Decent lecturer but does not go through challenging applied examples frequently. Recorded lectures are useful but he doesn't upload on time. Hw is mostly doable.
Great Professor, always willing to engage with students after/outside class. Sometimes falls behind on class logistics.

Lord Cundiff's first semester back at his alma mater, settling in to his new role. friendly, personable and passionate about optics. analysis.name: Jennifer Cummings

Dr. Cummings is a fantastic instructor, and I have never felt more engaged in a one-and-a-half hour lecture class. She's also great with questions.

Professor Cummings was very engaging and very receptive to questions both in the classroom as well as during office hours. analysis.name: William Currie

Do not recommend this class. Dr. Currie's explanations of things can be really confusing and he's very unclear of what you're supposed to learn for the exams. Speaking of which, the exams were very difficult and entirely based on how good your memory is, not your understanding of the concepts.

Profesor Currie took time to make a study guide for this semester. I personally love this class and I didn't think he was boring. The average for the first test was like 90% I think, and the second was 86% I think. You will need to have the book, but the homework is super easy.

analysis.name: Srdjan Cvjeticanin

Hes awesome. I didnt always know what he was talking about...(he gets lost in his own thoughts sometime, i think) and he goes of topic, but he comes back. Hes super smart and really nice. analysis.name: Anne Curzan

never made assignments or deadlines clear, made classes very stressful and gave a TON of homework and projects. graded critiques very harshly and would never give anyone an A. very rude as well when me and some classmates asked her for tools she was so passive aggressive about it. best to avoid...

Very approachable and the lectures are helpful, though a lot of people skip lecture and do fine (all the lecture slides are on ctools). I would definitely recommend taking a class with this professor.

It's easy to get an A though since the midterm is open note and the "final" is a paper

I was more stressed out in 3rd grade than I was in Ling106. Only 3 1-2 page assignments that take about 30 minutes and one final paper the entire semester. Those are the only ones though so make sure you proofread. I found a lot of the topics interesting even though I was only taking the class for credit, also Dr. Merchant and Sophie are very nice!

Really awesome and makes class really. As a Ling Major I do my best to get him as my lecturer because he's very nice and knowledgeable. He's great about answering questions in a very respectful manner and not afraid to say he doesn't know the answer. I will say he's sometimes nitpicky about grading but not to the point were you wont pass.

He is the best. Very chill and relaxed. Also has amazing lectures and class layouts with a couple of homework assignments, 1 midterm exam (open note), 1 essay (which counted as our final). Very open, and outgoing. He also has an amazing GSI named Sophie who is also very kind, knowledgeable, and approachable! Would 100% recommend him to others

I absolutely loved this class and the professor! Dr. Merchant and his GSI, Sophie, were both amazing teachers! analysis.name: David Doris

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Doris is one of the most intelligent professors I've had, and his penmanship is insane (You could tell by the way he introduced RFT at his lecture). I've never met a professor more passionate about their work. His lectures were more like slam poetry and you can tell that he wanted everyone to succeed. If you don't ask, you won't receive!

David Doris leaves a lasting impression. I took an upper level African Art class with 0 background in art history. He transformed my idea of a great teacher and made me wish I'd taken a class of his before my senior year. He's passionate, excited, knowledgeable, and always values students ideas. If you have the opportunity, take any class he offers

He is extremely smart and his lectures are more like slam poetry. It is important to go to every lecture to get an A, although it isn't mandatory. There is a lot of memorization for the exams. Their are a lot of long, required readings but they are very interesting.

David Doris is an amazing professor. He truly wants you to be inspired by this subject and see how it has impacted the world as a whole. As long as you take notes in lecture and memorize identifications, it is not difficult to get an A in the class.

Professor Dooley was my favorite professor I took this semester. Lots of busy work for his class but it's easy busy work and you have to study for exams in order to do well. He's a great guy who makes the class engaging.
